name: The Word of God
about: The KJV, the preservation of scripture, and rightly dividing it.

teachings.title: Compare spiritual with spiritual
teachings.summary: Doctrine cannot be built on a verse or two stripped of conditionals and context; scripture must be compared with scripture and let define itself, for God is not the author of confusion.
teachings.text:
Again, there are conditional statements and orders of operations here that tell us the specific context of what's being preached. As always, scripture references itself to provide the full picture. That's why we study the whole Bible, comparing spiritual with spiritual, not just taking a verse out of context, stripped of the conditionals and order, removed from supporting scripture.

You can't form doctrine around a verse or two and your assumptions and own reasonings, to fit doctrine you've decided on. You have to let God's word tell you what it means directly. God is not an author of confusion. The Bible defines itself and gives clear unambiguous statements for doctrine.

teachings.title: Cephas, by interpretation, a stone
teachings.summary: The Bible translates and defines itself, so Cephas means a stone, not the rock, and the whole Old Testament looked for the Christ.
teachings.text:
Next we get into the recruiting of the apostles. It's important to recognize that as Andrew tells his brother Simon, this is the Christ they were waiting for, because all faithful Jews were aware that God promised a savior. There's a false doctrine that the OT doesn't talk about Jesus when the entire thing is about Him.

The introduction of Peter contains the first reference of what Jesus meant when he renamed him; "*when Jesus beheld him, he said, Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone.*" Cephas/Peter means a stone, not 'rock.' (remember this when you're reading Matthew 16)

The Bible defines itself and the translation is done in the text itself, so as to have no mistake about it. John gives us the word and translation (by interpretation) repeatedly throughout his Gospel, and it's for good reason.

teachings.title: Lord, to whom shall we go
teachings.summary: God is not the author of confusion; scripture explains its own dark sayings, as Peter's confession sums up what Jesus meant.
teachings.text:
Just to wrap up, it's important to see that when asked, Peter shows that he gets it and believes. As some of the larger group of the disciples leave, he asks the 12 apostles if they too will leave, offended.

*Then Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life. And we believe and are sure that thou art that Christ, the Son of the living God*

A lot of people think that when God uses so-called dark sayings, or things that are difficult to understand on their own, that it's up to their own private interpretation or the interpretation of other men to tell them what it means. This couldn't be further from the truth.

God is not the author of confusion. God wants us to reason together with him. He wants us to understand and understanding, the Bible says, comes from God. That if we turn towards him, and read His word, we gain wisdom and in it, understanding.

But, just in case there's still any question, Jesus always turns to his disciples throughout the gospel and clearly lays it out or asks them questions and their response tells us what He means.

In two verses, Peter fully summarizes what Jesus meant: That He has the words of eternal life and that if you believe on them, that He is the Son of the living God and the Christ, you can obtain that gift.

But you have to have ears to hear, and eyes to see. You have to have sought truth, from God, and hearing it, believe His report.

teachings.title: Not my words but the word of God
teachings.summary: Those holding another gospel are refuted not by his words but by the whole word of God, read without pride so that it tells us its doctrine.
teachings.text:
There are many who profess to be Christian, but that believe another gospel, one of works, one of tradition of men, one that denies the power of Christ. And while I will rebuke and correct those in error, it's not my words that dispute them, but the word of God.

I have zero fear to post every word, jot and tittle, of the Bible to support my doctrine because it is not my own, but His.

When we read the whole word of God and listen without pride, without our own vain imaginings, without trying to fit the doctrine's we already believe to the word, but rather allow the word to tell us God's doctrines, we can come to understanding.

teachings.title: He that endureth to the end shall be saved from what
teachings.summary: The Spirit gives believers words under persecution, and saved in this passage means delivered from tribulation, so using it for preservation of the saints that can be lost is a false doctrine.
teachings.text:
Jesus teaches how the Holy Spirit, the inward dwelling aspect of the godhead, the Holy Ghost within, will lead them to remembrance all things, and give them what to say should they stand before council, persecuted for His name's sake.

This is a promise to all believers, that the comforter, the Holy Spirit indwelling can and will give us what to say in the hour of our tribulation. And that if we endure the trials and tribulations to the end, we shall be saved from them. Physically. Either by death of the flesh to heavenly reward, or by other means, such as the flood saving Noah from the wicked scoffers of his day, or just Lot delivered from the filth of Sodom.

Many take this verse out of context, and will claim "saved" always means justified by God, redeemed, made righteous. Most instances of the word saved in the Bible refer to rescue of the flesh, not salvation of the soul. Rightly dividing the word, we see that Jesus tells them what they are being saved *from,* and it's not Hell in this context, but the tribulations and persecution to come.

"Preservation of the saints" is a misapplication of the concept, and in many damnable heresies, is used to keep people from the truth of the Gospel, constantly worried the sins they commit after being born again are damning them, that if they backslide they lose their gift of eternal life. Depending on their own works to keep them justified, they remain perishing. It's a wicked false doctrine.

teachings.title: Saved, faith and damnation in context
teachings.summary: Words like saved, faith, damnation, justified and infidel often carry a present or earthly sense in the epistles, and reading them in context guards against twisting verses about salvation.
teachings.text: As a side note, that may help with understanding these passages; just as "saved" in scripture isn't always referring to justification by faith, but often physical salvation from danger, "faith" isn't always referring to the saving faith that we need to be redeemed. Often, especially in the epistles (which are written to believers), "faith" can refer to the deeper trust in God, or being faithful to His commands and expectations, or our own responsibility to others. And in the same manner, "condemnation," "damnation," "justified,"  or even "infidel" may be being applied in the present sense, regarding how one is looked at by others, not their spiritual condition in regards to eternal life. These are important distinctions, and understanding the context of the terms when they are used will save you when some try to cherry pick verses to come to a different meaning regarding salvation.

teachings.title: Prove all things by scripture
teachings.summary: False teachers who deny Christ's claims can only fool those who don't know the Bible, so wisdom comes by studying and comparing scripture with scripture, not by debate.
teachings.text:
*And they were in the way going up to Jerusalem; and Jesus went before them: and they were amazed; and as they followed, they were afraid. And he took again the twelve, and began to tell them what things should happen unto him, Saying, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man shall be delivered unto the chief priests, and unto the scribes; and they shall condemn him to death, and shall deliver him to the Gentiles: And they shall mock him, and shall scourge him, and shall spit upon him, and shall kill him: and the third day he shall rise again.*

Jesus spoke in parables to the masses, that only those who were truly meet for repentance could hear, but to those who believed and followed, He kept nothing from them, including the manner of His death and resurrection.

Again, there are false teachers out there that deny Jesus claimed to be God, or that He didn't preach on His death, burial and resurrection, and of course they are liars, deceiving those who don't know scripture. Like Satan tricking Eve by misquoting God's word, they can only fool those who don't know the Bible or believe it is true, who use arguments of man and are offended by scripture.

The Bible says to prove all things, comparing spiritual with spiritual, scripture to scripture.

*Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.*
...
*All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.*
...
*Teach me thy way, O LORD; I will walk in thy truth: unite my heart to fear thy name.*
...
*Thy word is true from the beginning: and every one of thy righteous judgments endureth for ever.*

And so we gain wisdom and knowledge by studying God's word. Not by endless argument and debate. Not by strivings about the law. Not by answering fools in their folly. But by the word of God.

teachings.title: Not everything a man says in scripture is so
teachings.summary: Abraham's claim that Sarah was his half-sister was said under duress, so we must test men's statements in the Bible by context and scripture.
teachings.text:
Now, when Abraham is outed by Abimelech, whom God visited in a dream to reveal the truth of Abraham's lie, Abimelech is wroth with anger, because he had taken Sarah *in the integrity of my heart and innocency of my hands*. He was actually a God-fearing king, of a righteous nation. He believed God would have killed him had He not kept the king from knowing Sarah, and commiting adultery. He was righteously angry at Abraham for putting himself and his nation at risk.

When confronted, Abraham says essentially, well, I was telling a half-truth, we are married but she's my half sister. Daughter of his father Terah and a different mother.

Now this is held dogmatically by many, that Abraham and Sarah were half-siblings, sharing the same father. But this is the only instance where this appears in scripture, and it's Abraham caught in one lie by an angry king, told under duress. We cannot assume she is Terah's daughter just because Abraham says it. Unless God or someone in the Spirit speaking for God says it, we have to look at context to see if what they're saying is true, or the truth from their perspective, or possibly a lie or rationalization.

But, Abraham does make the claim. It is possible that he's telling the truth, but it's not enough to draw a definitive conclusion.

teachings.title: Onan's Sin Was Denying Seed to His Brother
teachings.summary: Onan was slain not for the act itself but for refusing to raise seed to his dead brother as God's law required, a passage commonly misread.
teachings.text:
Today on Judah Springer....

Judah, the son of Israel who had led his brothers to sell Joseph to bondage, is not a good guy. One of the reasons the brothers hated the young brother Joseph was that he brought an evil report back to their father, and we see from this synopsis of Judah's life, there was plenty of evil to report.

Judah falls in with a rough crowd of heathens, being best friends with an Adullamite. He marries a Canaanite woman and bears sons wicked enough to be slain by the Lord. The eldest, Er, isn't detailed what all he did, but it was wicked enough to get God's attention.

And when his wife was left childless by his death, Judah does try to do what is right by her and give her a child by his son Onan. This custom mirrors the law given by God to Moses.

**Deuteronomy 25:5**
*If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband's brother shall go in unto her, and take her to him to wife, and perform the duty of an husband's brother unto her.*

This is the law and what's right in the eyes of God.

Of course, we see in the Gospels that the Sadducees use this to tempt Jesus;

**Matthew 22**
*23 The same day came to him the Sadducees, which say that there is no resurrection, and asked him,*

*24 Saying, Master, Moses said, If a man die, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.*

*25 Now there were with us seven brethren: and the first, when he had married a wife, deceased, and, having no issue, left his wife unto his brother:*

*26 Likewise the second also, and the third, unto the seventh.*

*27 And last of all the woman died also.*

*28 Therefore in the resurrection whose wife shall she be of the seven? for they all had her.*

*29 Jesus answered and said unto them, Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God.*

*30 For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven.*

*31 But as touching the resurrection of the dead, have ye not read that which was spoken unto you by God, saying,*

*32 I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.*

*33 And when the multitude heard this, they were astonished at his doctrine.*

It is in this context we see Judah offering Onan unto his daughter-in-law Tamar. But Onan refuses to give a son to his dead brother, knowing Tamar but spilling his seed on the ground. For this wicked act, God slays Onan as well.

Many think Onan's sin was pulling out, in general. That's not the case, it was the specific act of denying seed to his dead brothers wife, breaking the law and dishonoring everyone involved.

*And Onan knew that the seed should not be his; and it came to pass, when he went in unto his brother's wife, that he spilled it on the ground, lest that he should give seed to his brother.*
*And the thing which he did displeased the Lord: wherefore he slew him also*.

This misunderstanding of the scriptures has led to the term Onanism to describe a sin of not completing in a woman, and is often associated with masturbation.

The more you know.

teachings.title: Revelation Is About Christ, Not Geopolitics
teachings.summary: Like all scripture Revelation centres on Christ, explains its own mysteries so it is not too hard to read, and names churches plural, not a universal church.
teachings.text:
We see here in chapter one that, like the rest of scripture, the focus is on Christ Jesus and the spiritual things of God. When we read any of the Bible, we should keep this our focus. Comparing spiritual things with spiritual. It greatly helps with rightly dividing the word of God.

John writes that it comes "*from Jesus Christ, who is the faithful witness, and the first begotten of the dead, and the prince of the kings of the earth. Unto him that loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood, And hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father; to him be glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen. Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him. Even so, Amen."*

This is what it's all about. It isn't about geopolitics. It's not about which earthly nation or events we want it to be. It's not a warning to those "left behind." It is written to be a blessing to the saved that we may know God's will in the last days, the honor and glory of Jesus and His triumph of the resurrection, His reign, wrath, judgement and victory. We are called simply witness to His glory, amen.

Lord Jesus, who we are repeatedly told is "*Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end,"* He *which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty*.

John describes the vision of Jesus He has:  *the Son of man, clothed with a garment down to the foot, and girt about the paps with a golden girdle.*
*His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow; and his eyes were as a flame of fire; And his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace; and his voice as the sound of many waters.*
*And he had in his right hand seven stars: and out of his mouth went a sharp twoedged sword: and his countenance was as the sun shineth in his strength.*

He is radiant, fitted with a golden girdle, hair white, feet bronzed, and from His mouth comes the Word, a two-edged sword.

**Hebrews 4:12**
*For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.*

Some heretical blacks use this passage to claim Jesus is black. It's foolishness. His feet are like brass as if they'd been burned in a furnace, not natural pigmentation. Again, it is applying natural man things to what is spiritual that leads people to nonsense doctrine.

John says as he turned to witness Christ he sees seven stars and seven golden candlesticks. This is one of the many symbolic illustrations we will see as we go through Revelation. And these are the kinds of things that false prophets seize upon to claim that the book is too mysterious to understand directly. That one needs some gnostic process to understand. Yet, as we read on we see that each mystery is explained. Jesus says to John regarding the 7 stars/golden candlesticks;

*The mystery of the seven stars which thou sawest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches.*

We aren't left to wonder about much. There are some hard passages and dark sayings contained in Revelation, but more often than not, they are explained in the narrative. God is not the author of confusion. Trust in the Spirit. So much of this is incredibly straightforward, it is a shame Satan has made people afraid to read Revelation. That confusion the devil has sown in the world keeps Christians from the blessing that is found in it.

So, now heading into chapter 2, recall that the 7 stars are the angels of the 7 churches, and the 7 candlesticks are the churches themselves.

Note, churches, plural. The idea of a single universal church is not biblical. They were independent and Christ led, New Testament churches from the beginning.

teachings.title: Revelation 12 Tells It Three Times
teachings.summary: Revelation intentionally repeats events, and chapter 12 tells the same vision three times, which helps in understanding it.
teachings.text:
One of the difficulties people have with reading the book of Revelation is understanding that several times throughout the book, certain themes or events are repeated, intentionally by God. How the book is split to go over the prophecy given us from 6 to 11, in chapters 12 through 19. And then we're given additional details of the white throne judgment and the new heaven in the new earth in chapters 20 through 22. In a like manner, Revelation 12 tells the same thing three different times.

It's the same vision, but we are given slight changes in detail throughout the chapter that indicate that it tells the story of the woman, travailing im birth, and  the devil seeking to devour her seed. That is Christ, and making war on those who believe on Him.

We can see in verses 1 through 7, 8 through 11 and versus 12 through 17, we see what are essentially the same events told three different times. From the prophecy and birth of Christ to the persecution of the saints in the tribulation after the fall of Satan and his hosts.

It still can be daunting but I have found as I have looked at it with these repetitions in mind, it can become a bit easier to understand.

teachings.title: Revelation Tells the End Twice
teachings.summary: Comparing chapter 11 with 16 shows Revelation retells the end times twice, and preterism and other systems fail because they do not make the Bible the final authority.
teachings.text:
I want to add a quick note regarding the chronology of all of this, and how we can know that the first 11 chapters of Revelation and the second 11 chapters are retelling end times events.

If you look back in chapter 11, it's given to us that the kingdoms of this world have become Christ's.

*The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever.*

But we see here in chapter 16, that the beast is still on his throne and is sending out evil spirits to convince all of the subordinate kings to gather their armies at Armageddon.

*And the fifth angel poured out his vial upon the seat of the beast; and his kingdom was full of darkness; and they gnawed their tongues for pain,*

If you have spent any time looking for answers in end times Bible prophecy, you will have come across a whole host of YouTube videos and internet posts that purport to give the chronology and explain the symbolism.

Of course, the dispensationalist version of events is the most prevalent today, but there's also the post-trib post-wrath version of end times Bible prophecy that's called the classical version. That conflates all of it and lists the seven seals and trumpets and vials as essentially the same thing, God's wrath. And that his people are not spared the wrath but forced to go through both the Great Tribulation and these plagues.

There are also those who say that the trumpets and the vials are the same judgments. Or that rather than happening concurrently happen 7 trump's and then 7 vials after the other. They don't rightly divide the word of God and will say that Revelation is all one continuous chronology.

But we can know simply by looking at scripture and comparing it to scripture precisely how it is divided, and how the order of events fits with other scripture such as the Olivette discourse given by Jesus in Matthew, Mark and Luke.

So when scripture in chapter 11 tells us that the Millennial reign is here, but then in chapter 16, we are told that the beast still has control of the kingdoms of the earth, it's easy to tell that this is simply a second run through of the events. Reiterating key points for our benefit.

It's also pretty clear, as we go through the book of Revelation, that the idea that this is already happened, that this was fulfilled in 70 AD (which is 20 years prior to the writing of Revelation), is all absurd. Anyone pushing that false doctrine cannot answer how it is that none of these great plagues and celestial events have ever taken place. Or explain how it is that Jesus is ruling and reigning with an iron rod today. That Satan is bound in Hell.

Far too many people who profess to be Christians settle on a theory or doctrine and then seek validation for it from other men. Rather than going to scripture and seeing what God has to say which dispels every false doctrine.

Those who don't treat the Bible as the final authority and the complete and perfect word of God will always be left struggling to come up with rationalizations to explain away the contradictions that arise from their false doctrines.

teachings.title: One Gospel to Romans and Hebrews
teachings.summary: Paul teaches the same gospel to Gentiles and Hebrews from what each knew, and the 66 books are to be taken as one testimony rather than cherry picked.
teachings.text:
It's interesting to point out the distinction between the epistle to the Romans and to the Hebrews, where when writing to the Gentiles, Paul lays out doctrine based on their understanding, starting first with the Revelation of God through creation and his wrath and the conviction of the holy spirit, in our conscience. Conscience. Law written upon our heart that man may have no excuse. He then moves on to idols and reprobation, and the need for salvation.

Here in Hebrews, he establishes these doctrines immediately, using scripture that the Hebrews are already familiar with, concepts that they've already absorbed.

It's the same gospel and the same message and both inspired. And we are blessed having the whole word of God preserved for all time at our disposal that all of His doctrines, and the words of the prophets and of Christ. And written to the early church are laid out for us in one place, in one location that we may understand.

Far too many claiming to be Christian cherry pick and weave through verses that they twist to fit their preconceived notions and agendas. But God's word is laid out as such that it is a hole, spread over 66 books but meant to be taken as a single testimony.

teachings.title: Some shall not taste death: the transfiguration
teachings.summary: Jesus' saying that some would see the kingdom was fulfilled eight days later at the transfiguration, so lifting it out of context to support preterism is a failure to rightly divide.
teachings.text:
Now, Jesus ends all this by saying:

*But I tell you of a truth, there be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the kingdom of God.*

And immediately, Luke brings us to the transfiguration of Jesus on the mountain:

*And it came to pass about an eight days after these sayings, he took Peter and John and James, and went up into a mountain to pray.*

So, follow that. He tells them that some of them shall see Him come into His glory, glimpsing the kingdom of Heaven before they taste death, and it came to pass eight days later that three of them do just that.

This passage messes with people, where they come away with some kind of preterism or weird doctrines, because they don't rightly divide the word of God. They take a verse out of a larger narrative, stripped of context and then use their own foolish logic, try to make it make sense. Others who aren't familiar with the word pick up these errors and strange doctrines and repeat them. That's why we read all of it, in context, comparing scripture with scripture.

And so, Peter, James and John, the three Apostles who are closest to Jesus, witness Jesus transfigured in His glory, with Moses and Elijah who appear in glory. They are a witness to the Kingdom, out of due time.

It is often brushed over or minimized that Jesus was discussing His coming trials in Jerusalem with these great prophets of God, the culmination of God's will that these men preached in their day. What a conversation to be witness to, and add to that the understanding of the glory that awaits us in the Kingdom to come.

Peter, who always says the wrong thing, suggests building tabernacles for Jesus and these saints, as he attempts to process what they'd witnessed. And a cloud overtakes them and envelopes them, and the voice of the Father says to them "*This is my beloved Son: hear him.*"

Peter and the brothers, James and John are witnesses to the presence of God, Christ in His glory, with the glorified Old Testament saints with everlasting life, not in a vision, but present with them on the mountain. They've seen the Kingdom of God.

teachings.title: Study to shew thyself approved
teachings.summary: Paul's writings are scripture that the unlearned wrest to their destruction, so believers must study and rightly divide the word, comparing scripture with scripture, to guard against false doctrine.
teachings.text:
You can see how Paul builds an argument block by block, in one long thought that establishes the foundation of the idea he wants to convey. It is careful and methodical and of the Spirit in its simplicity, but confounding those who don't believe with its dense structure, making his writings a snare for those who don't actually hold the faith that he uses as the foundations for his epistles. Something that Peter addresses in his own epistle to the churches of Asia:

**2 Peter 3:13-17**
*Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness. Wherefore, beloved, seeing that ye look for such things, be diligent that ye may be found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless. And account that the longsuffering of our Lord is salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you; As also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things; in which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction.Ye therefore, beloved, seeing ye know these things before, beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness.*

Peter both acknowledges Paul's standing as an Apostle, his writings as scripture, and that what he writes confounds the unlearned and unstable, the babe in Christ or the unbelieving. Peter appeals to them, saying since they have the faith, they should beware being taken by those who wrest with scripture out of ignorance or unbelief, by false doctrines pulled from the complexity of Paul's writings, as well as scripture in general.

As Paul writes in **2 Timothy 2:15**
*Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.*

We study scripture for God's approval, and to not be ashamed, that is taken astray, caught off guard by an argument we don't have an answer for, being misled by those who wrestle with scripture to pull out false doctrines, etc. To be like the Thessalonians;

**Acts 17:11**
*These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.*

**1 Corinthians 2:13**
*Which things also we speak, not in the words which man's wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual.*

This is how we grow in grace and peace. This is how we protect ourselves from false doctrines or doubtful disputations by the unlearned and unstable, and the false prophets bringing another gospel. This is how we please God. This is how we can stand stedfast on our faith not being ashamed by naysayers or mockers. This is how we share our faith to others that they may receive the same forgiveness and grace that we have.

So, as we study to be approved by God, it is important to get how the Spirit leads Paul to build his case, his outline for the theology that comes from our salvation. The implications for living in the faith that we share.

teachings.title: Romans 2 answers a rhetorical opponent
teachings.summary: In Romans 2 Paul is not addressing Jews in the church but answering a rhetorical Jewish objector, part of one methodical argument across the epistle.
teachings.text:
Answering a question with a brother about **Romans 2** had me really rethink something that I missed, and it clarified a lot of the misunderstanding around the chapter, specifically who it is written to.

Because of the language Paul uses, specifically at the end of the chapter, many assume he is directly addressing Jews there, despite the greetings in chapter 1 being to the church in Rome, which are Gentiles. In my study, I did what a lot of people do and just squared the circle by saying basically the church has both Jews and Greeks (which is likely true, but irrelevant to what Paul is doing).

The entire epistle is a general one, and all believers are the audience. But there is a default understanding that some of it is actually targeted to Jews, in the church, based especially on the last half of chapter 2.

But it's not.

Paul's not writing to Jews. He's writing a rhetorical method of argument that addresses common points made about Gentiles, then Jews, in a methodical way.

It's part of the larger argument that he's making in the epaitle. It isn't literally him saying to the Jew the things he says, but addressing questions often raised by Jews against Christians who were preaching that Gentiles were now made accessible to the Gospel of Grace. When Paul says "O man..." is like when James says "a man may say..."

It's a method of rhetoric common in the era. Anticipating and answering objections to stipulate certain points.

And so after establishing that Gentiles, despite being pagans and many reprobate and given over, with no excuse, given up to all unrighteousness, have access salvation in Christ, Paul continues to hammer Jewish objections to this idea.

*Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God, And knowest his will, and approvest the things that are more excellent, being instructed out of the law*...This is addressed to a rhetorical Jewish opponent who would make these claims, not specifically "to Jews."

Chapter three changes to 3rd person, because it was always the arguments being made, not the audience being addressed.

*What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision? Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God. For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect?*

Having chapters and verse helps to quickly reference scripture, but the breaks can cause confusion when a larger point is being made. Go back and read the entire epistle in one go, and consider it's Paul, in the Spirit, making several arguments, methodically. Not telling Jews one thing and Gentiles another.

teachings.title: Let the Bible tell us what it is discussing
teachings.summary: Secondary dogmas forced out of a text miss the point, for the Bible is clear on doctrine and given for winning souls, not winning fights online.
teachings.text:
We have to be very careful in letting the Bible tell us what's being discussed, to understand the context and not wrestle something else out of it. And it angers a lot of people who have settled into one side or another on a secondary or tertiary doctrine, and seek justification from scripture for it, to make dogmatic statements.

I have noticed that so many of these dogmas, and the binaries that form from them, are carnal and incidental to the larger point being made. And so people miss the forest for the trees.

When I have applied this form of exegesis to pet theories in scripture, even when I agree with the theory in whole or in part, people get angry. "Both sides" foam at the mouth over this. Labels of heresy and compromise abound. But in my view the Bible is very clear on doctrine and things that have to be forced out of the text aren't worthy of being dogmatic. Simple as.

The Bible is not for our eisegesis to win fights online. Especially about carnal things. It is for the winning of souls.

teachings.title: Destroyed for lack of knowledge
teachings.summary: Confusing passages are understood by comparing scripture with scripture, and Satan tempts by making us doubt or by our ignorance of the word, so Christians must study it daily.
teachings.text:
This is a pretty deep story, and it can be confusing because it relies on knowledge of scripture to discern what exactly is going on. Especially when the sin of David is not spelled out and the account in **1 Chronicles 21** adds Satan into the mix.

But like anything else in the Bible, the answer to our confusion is found by comparing scripture with scripture. Too often, Christians can be led away with foolish doctrine because they don't know the word of God.

Satan will tempt us when God allows it, and often our reaction is used by God to get our attention, to show us our error. To give us a chance to get right, as in this case. God always provides a means of escape;

**1 Corinthians 10:13**
*There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.*

And the means of Satan's testing begins with making us either question the word of God (*Ye, hath God said?*) or taking advantage of our ignorance that we may be led into sin;

**Hosea 4:6**
*My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.*

The law of God is perfect. It serves a wonderful purpose. It allows us to have knowledge and understanding of the mind of the Lord, and His will for us.

People get bogged down in theology and vain philosophy of men, and lose sight of the purpose of the word. Christians should study to be approved before God, reading His word daily, our daily bread. The words of eternal life given to us by the inspiration of God.

teachings.title: The great things of my law counted strange
teachings.summary: Today Bible fundamentalism is mocked as strange by seminary-trained scholars, but like Israel's traditions of men this is folly, so we must study to be approved of God and compare scripture with scripture.
teachings.text:
*I have written to him the great things of my law, but they were counted as a strange thing.*

Today, Biblical fundamentalism is seen as a strange thing, an atavistic anachronism. A throwback to a time where people weren't as "enlightened." Where the "critical text reading" of scripture didn't exist. Where common people just didn't know that the Bible "isn't literal," that it was outdated and written to the "culture at the time."

Today, we have such "wisdom," from our intellectual betters, graduates of Seminary School, who studied Greek for a few semesters, and know that the average Christian just cannot understand such archaic language and concepts.

Those thinking themselves wise became fools. The law of God became a strange thing to them, and so they lean on their own understanding.

This is why we must study to be approved by God, not men. To compare spiritual things with spiritual. To search the scriptures to see if things are so. To know God and His word, and in the Spirit come to see His wisdom and judgment, and not our own.

Israel followed man's wisdom. They added idols and icons to venerate in their worship, set their own standards for priests, set their own holy days, and feasts, their own standards. Teaching for commandments the doctrines of men. Holding scripture out as a strange thing, and instead trusting in tradition. Trading the unchanging rock of God for shifting sands.

And this sowing the wind, they reap the whirlwind.

teachings.title: Read Old Testament prophecy through the New
teachings.summary: Differences between OT and NT prophecy are what could have been versus what will be, so we should scrap Darby and Scofield and read the OT through the NT.
teachings.text:
And so the implications of this Theory are broad and deep. It would apply to just about every covenant promise made with conditions to the people of Israel in the Old Testament and any differences between Old Testament prophecy of end times and New.

Ezekiel's Battle of Gog and Magog has some different aspects to it than Revelation's. They still happen, As described by John from the Revelation given him, and the difference is what could have been versus what will be now that the Old Testament is done away with. Necessary changes.

The millennial Kingdom references in Old Testament prophecy very slightly from what we are clearly taught in the new New Testament.

All of the little nuances and seeming contradictions and places where people trying to rightly divide the word of God are jamming Square pegs into round holes to make the prophecies we are given in the New Testament fit with the promises given in the Old.

One of the evils of dispensationalism is that it has so badly blinded everyone, but even we who reject it are so used to dealing with everything on their terms. What if that's just a huge mistake. What if we need to scrap everything that comes out of Darby and Schofield and dispensationalism entirely, and take a new view of the Old Testament through the lens of the New?

teachings.title: John 3:13: the Son of man which is in heaven
teachings.summary: The KJV's John 3:13 keeps that Christ was in heaven while on earth, while modern versions cut it and so feed dispensationalist error.
teachings.text:
Real quick John 3 point: Check out KJV v Non Inspired Version in verse 13

<13> And no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven.

vs

<13> No one has ever gone into heaven except the one who came from heaven—the Son of Man.

You see the problem? All the OT saints are in heaven, spiritually. Enoch was translated up into heaven. Ezekiel was taken up. David's soul was "taken up to heaven" while his corruptible body was entombed. But to read the HIV version, none were. It's wicked and how the dispensationalists get around their rejection of OT grace and calling upon the name of the Lord.

teachings.title: If thou believest with all thine heart
teachings.summary: Acts 8:37 gives the order of salvation, believing that Jesus is the Son of God and then baptism, which is why modern versions remove or doubt it.
teachings.text:
Now, after Philip has given him the gospel and shown him, out of the Bible the truth of Jesus Christ, the eunuch asks what hinders him from being baptized in the water the caravan had come to, and Philip answers with pure doctrine;

*If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest.*

*And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.*

This is the Gospel. This is how salvation works. This is the order of things, and baptism is but a public expression of the salvation that came from belief.

And so Acts 8:37 is either removed or footnoted into doubt by all modern perversions of the Bible. The simplicity of the Gospel, that we are saved by our belief in this truth that Jesus is the Son of God, the Christ who saves us by His perfect work, as God promised from the foundation of the world.

The removal or doubt-casting on this verse, the clearest and most explicit example of 1-on-1 soul winning thus far in the New Testament, can only be done for one reason, and to serve one agenda; Satan's.

We see the eunuch saved, baptized and Philip carried away by the Holy Spirit, leaving one of the most powerful men in Ethiopia joyfully proclaiming Jesus Christ.

teachings.title: Tongues, prophecy and the preserved English word
teachings.summary: Tongues were languages and prophecy is preaching scripture to understanding, so services in a dead language, back-to-the-Greek scholars and Ruckmanites all err, and God has preserved His word in English in the KJV needing no outside interpreter.
teachings.text:
Paul continues his teaching to the Corinthians on spiritual gifts, having put in place the doctrine that we shouldn't covet and envy those who have received talents to the edification of the church that differ from ours, that all in the body serve the same head, that head being Jesus and through Him, the Father. Then making the case that being charitable, the love for others that God expressed to us, and Christ demonstrated on the cross, then we've a better gift than even those the Holy Ghost bestowed on many in this time. Specifically the ability to speak and understand foreign tongues, or languages.

The Bible is clear that this is the meaning. Not the nonsense gibberish of the pentecostal heathen. No where in the Bible does the term "speaking in tongues" exist (unless you read one of the perverted modern versions that sow false doctrine with confusion so often).

This gift is rather the use of those who can interpret or prophesy scripture to those who speak another tongue.

Like the Apostles and disciples on Pentecost, who spoke the Gospel to those pilgrims from all over the world, in Jerusalem for the feast. They spoke to understanding, and it amazed the crowd and acted as a sign, bringing thousands to belief as they heard the word of God in their native language.

Prophecy in the Bible is the preaching of scripture, and bringing the relevance of the word of God to the people. It is giving the Gospel to the unbelieving. It is teaching the law. It is relevant preaching to the building up of the church. It is the advice of proverbs taught at a mother's knee. It is the exhorting of the pulpit to the flock.

And if any of this be done in a language none of the hearers understand, as Paul says in chapter 13, it is of *sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.*

This goes for false religion that gives entire services in a dead language. It is to no one's edification but the speaker.

This goes for the "You must return to the Hebrew! You must return to the Greek! God's word is impossible to understand in English!" nonsense of puffed up "scholars" who take pride in their private interpretation and sowing confusion among the people to show how learned they are.

This goes to the Ruckmanites who take the preservation of the Word in the KJV to be a further revelation that is more perfect than the Greek and Hebrew, which is nonsense.

Paul says that if you have a gift of knowing a language that can be used for interpretation to the person being reached with the Gospel then use it, but not to show off to the believers who cannot understand it, which seems the case in Corinth.

As Pentecost showed us, God's word is powerful in any language, and in every tongue God, who is not the author of confusion can make His word known.

Verse 26 he wonders how it is so many in Corinth are puffed up by claims of their own doctrines and revelations and psalms, and strange tongues, etc. They apparently were many among them who, in covetousness and pride were deceitfully inventing whole doctrines and aping gifts they did not have, or bragging about gifts they were given and wasting them.

As for tongues, today we have the inspired Word of God, preserved by the Spirit, in English in the KJV. And we should be grateful that we need no one to tell us it's lingual meaning, as every word and term is defined in itself. There is no need to appeal to a concordance or other work of an unsaved man to explain to us the plain meaning of His scripture.

teachings.title: Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures
teachings.summary: Jesus' constant rebuke was that men knew not the scriptures, and casting doubt on God's complete, preserved word is Satan's work from Eden onward.
teachings.text:
Having struck out with the Pharisees, next come the Sadducees, worldly Jews who denied the spiritual things of God, the resurrection, Heaven and Hell, trying to trip Jesus up with a foolish hypothetical that they thought would expose Him to ridicule and show, using the logic of the natural man, the folly and contradictions they thought existed in God's word.

In the hypothetical of the woman married to seven brothers, in keeping with the law of Moses, they ask to whom she would be married to in the Resurrection (which they didn't believe in).

And Jesus answers their bad faith question in a familiar way. As He has repeatedly said to the other's attempts to trap Him, they don't know the scriptures or they wouldn't ask such foolishness;

*Jesus answered and said unto them, Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God. For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven.*

*But as touching the resurrection of the dead, have ye not read that which was spoken unto you by God, saying, I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.*

Whether it was Satan tempting Him in the wilderness, His disciples and their misunderstanding, the Pharisees and Sadducees and their rhetorical traps, Jesus most common rebuke is that they know not the scriptures. "Have you not read...?"

The answer to all our questions are found in God's word. If we read it in faith, the Spirit gives us understanding.

All knowledge and wisdom come from God, and His complete, inspired and preserved word available to all who seek it.

Those who claim we don't have access to the perfect and preserved word of God, who cast doubts on its veracity, its origins, its content, who add or remove whole verses, change doctrine, introduce contradictions and sow confusion, are doing the work of Satan, whose first act against man, enticing Eve to sin, was casting doubt on God's word.

For where there is doubt or uncertainty, there is no power. And without the power, there is no salvation. And so Lucifer's goal of damning man is reached.

This is why we are instructed to study all things, seeking to be approved unto God, not man. Comparing spiritual with spiritual. Proving all things whether they be true. And believing that God - who cannot lie, who is not the author of confusion, who promises that it is His job to keep His word preserved for all time, is true and to be believed when He promises us eternal life in His Son.

teachings.title: All scripture given by inspiration of God
teachings.summary: 2 Timothy 3 teaches that all scripture is inspired, preserved and sufficient for doctrine, so independent fundamental Baptist churches drawing doctrine from scripture alone are the only way.
teachings.text:
Paul, again in his final days, knowing he won't see Asia Minor and the churches he planted there or the evangelists like Timothy he's laid hands on and sent out, again, and having several of them turn from him in fear of persecution and shame of Paul's bonds, and several false teachers creep in to the churches to lead men shipwreck, is laying out the foundational doctrines for Timothy to remember and pass on. There's an urgency that allows Paul, in the Spirit to be as concise and precise as possible. It makes second Timothy one of the densest and deep books, despite it's brevity.

Here we see, in order, the Reprobate Doctrine, the names of Pharoah's court wizards (Jannes and Jambres), how reprobates will grow worse and worse over time, infiltrating houses, leading people astray, especially women. That God will give them what they deserve in the end.

We learn the sound doctrines taught of Paul, purpose, faith, longsuffering, charity, patience, and the assurance that ALL who live Godly in Christ will see persecution. Tribulations and trouble for His name's sake.

That faith comes from hearing and hearing by the Word of God. That scriptures make us wise unto salvation by faith in Jesus Christ. Faith alone, in Christ alone. Further, that *All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, thoroughly furnished unto all good works.*

We get out doctrine from scripture. No other source, but the word of God. It is perfect, meaning complete. It is inspired. It is preserved. If it weren't preserved, how could it thoroughly furnish a man of God unto salvation through faith? Unto good works?

These doctrines are either denied or added to by denominations today. They deny reprobation. They deny salvation by faith alone. They deny scripture is preserved, inspired or even necessary for doctrine.

Even prot denominations that claim Sola Fide and Sola Scripta will add works to salvation and writings of "reformers" and church fathers to their faithless theology.

Biblical Fundamentalism is the only way. New Testament churches, independent, pastor led, engaged in preaching the Gospel to every creature, a believer's baptism, a congregation of believers studying the scriptures to be approved by God, charitable to the brethren, judge to the fatherless, honoring elders and widows indeed. Eating communal suppers, in Jesus name. Tithing that those who work to the edification of the assembly are given their due.

Awaiting the return of Jesus to save us out of great tribulation, and bring the wrath of God upon the wicked and profane. The rapture and resurrection of the saints. The millennial reign. The marriage feast of the lamb. Giving glory to God forever and ever. Amen.

Everything else is doctrines of devils, having the appearance of righteousness, a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof. From these, the Bible says, flee.

teachings.title: Pure Words Purified Seven Times
teachings.summary: Psalm 12 teaches that God's pure, preserved words cut off the proud lips of the wicked, and he notes the KJV as the seventh major English translation.
teachings.text:
One of the shortest Psalms, the theme is entirely about words, the wickeds' and God's.

There is a lack of godly men and a fall of the faithful, because they speak vanity, flattery, and lies (a double heart).

The Lord shall cut off all the lips and tongues doing this, speaking proud things. Quoting the proud and wicked "With our tongue will we prevail; our lips are our own: who is lord over us?"

The wicked and their Talmudic reasoning, pilpul, theologies of men, their vain and foolish ideas believe they are triumphant over God. But David, writing in the Spirit says that the Lord shall reprove them. Expose them.

Because the words of the Lord are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times.

(BTW, the KJV is the 7th of the major translations into English, and considered the best)

Thou shall keep them, o Lord , thou shall preserve them. From this generation for ever.

It's God's word. Perfect and inspired and preserved. That's what cuts off the lips and tongues of the wicked. The liars. The proud. Those speaking vanities.

And praise God we have His preserved word, because the wicked walk in every side when the vilest men are exalted.

teachings.title: The burned scroll written again
teachings.summary: When Jehoiakim burned the scroll God had it written again, showing that His word cannot be destroyed though the false church has burned both manuscripts and the men who held them.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 24:35**
*Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.*

In **Jeremiah 36**, the word of the Lord comes upon the prophet telling him to write the words of prophecy God had given him in a scroll, and to have the word of God read in the temple and to the people of Jerusalem. With the aid of a scribe named Baruch, he does just that. And when Baruch reads it in the temple, during a declared feast to the Lord, saying Babylon would certainly destroy Judah and leave the land desolate, it pricked the ears of certain princes of the kingdom, who knowing the danger to the prophet and scribe, told them to go into hiding while they conveyed the word to the king. And when the king heard it, he cut up the scroll and cast it into the fire and indeed sought their lives, but God hid them.

And God said to write the words again in another scroll, the scripture not being hid, impossible to destroy. Because the word of God is spirit and life, not the paper it is confined to, but the truth that is from everlasting to everlasting.

Just as in the centuries since Pentecost, as New Testament Christians and their churches, led of the Spirit, wrote down the word of God, and just as the apostate false church sought to destroy those scrolls and manuscripts, and to kill the servants of God who held them. Often burning the man and the parchment together. But God's word endures. And the word endures because there are always wicked men, like Jehoiakim, and vile deeds to be preached against. And the truth of God is eternal.

**Psalm 12:6-8**
*The words of the Lord are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times. Thou shalt keep them, O Lord, thou shalt preserve them from this generation for ever. The wicked walk on every side, when the vilest men are exalted.*

teachings.title: Beware extrabiblical books
teachings.summary: Books lost to us were not needed, and seeking apocrypha and forgeries like Enoch snares believers, so read the Bible many times before histories.
teachings.text:
After this short story, we are given an account of the victory against the Amorites, through the power of the Lord delivering them. And the king of Bashan, who went against them and perished.

And the children of Israel took their cities and killed everyone of the people.

*Thus Israel dwelt in the land of the Amorites.*

There appears reference of a book of the wars of the Israelites, and it is mentioned in Exodus and may be referred to in some of the prophets. Tales or songs sung of the victories the children of Israel had in this time. But that it's lost to us means it ultimately wasn't important to us. There are similar mentions in Kings and Chronicles to other accounts recorded.

But we get the gist from the canonical books.

There is an itch some have where they desperately want to know these things, and seek out extrabiblical sources and are prone to believing Jewish fables offered as truth. It is a fine line to walk and discernment is a must. But for most seeking truth outside of the Bible, it becomes a trap and a snare.

Just look at the weight some give to apocrypha. And to clear forgeries like the "Gospel" of Andrew and the "Book of Enoch." People get derailed, even saved Christians, by studying things that had they been important, would have been inspired and preserved by God in His word.

Until someone has read the Bible multiple times, I really suggest staying away from histories and extrabiblical accounts and sources. Build up the knowledge of the Lord and the Spirit will provide discernment.

teachings.title: Ye shall not add unto the word
teachings.summary: God's statutes are for our good, and the command not to add to or diminish His word condemns the false versions that do so today.
teachings.text:
There's a lot of doctrine in this, the 4th chapter of **Deuteronomy**, and a lot to digest. Moses speaking to the assembly of Israel, after successfully destroying two of the Canaanite kings and their kingdoms on the east side of the Jordan, about to enter the promised land. Recounting the events leading up to this moment and retelling the law as given by God to their fathers, 40 years earlier.

Starting immediately with the understanding that they have the statutes and judgments of God, given them that they may live. The reminder that the commandments of God are given for our benefit, that it be well with us. That by following His precepts we prolong our lives. The Lord God has blessed us with this knowledge and understanding.

Many professing Christians today minimize the civil laws of God, acting as if they were for that time and place, or dismissing them with the carnal ordinances and sacrifices done away with in Christ. But they do so to their own destruction. As Paul writes in **Ephesians 6:2-3**;

*Honour thy father and mother; which is the first commandment with promise; That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.*

This is the first commandment with promise, but hardly the last. We will see similar promises of God that following His law is to our own benefit throughout **Deuteronomy**.

*Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it, that ye may keep the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you.*

Relevant to us today, the diminishing of God's word continues to be Satan's main line of attack. "Yea, hath God said..?"

**Revelation 22:19**
*And if any man shall take away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part out of the book of life, and out of the holy city, and from the things which are written in this book.*

The recording of the law begins and ends with the same admonition. Yet so many today will cling to false versions of God's word that remove and add to it, seeking to diminish from it, that man might fail to keep God's commands.

teachings.title: Seven hundred or seven thousand horsemen
teachings.summary: The seeming discrepancy between 2 Samuel 8 and 1 Chronicles 18 is explained by comparing the accounts, and modern versions that alter it show a lack of faith in the preservation of the word.
teachings.text:
Critics of the Authorized Version of the King James Bible, and nonbelievers alike, will point to an apparent discrepancy in the telling of these events taken from **2 Samuel 8** and its parallel in **1 Chronicles 18**, a matter of horsemen and chariots.

*David smote also Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to recover his border at the river Euphrates. And David took from him a thousand chariots, and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen: and David houghed all the chariot horses, but reserved of them for an hundred chariots.*

vs

*And David smote Hadarezer king of Zobah unto Hamath, as he went to stablish his dominion by the river Euphrates. And David took from him a thousand chariots, and seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen: David also houghed all the chariot horses, but reserved of them an hundred chariots*.

The difference between the two numbers is "corrected" in many modern versions, while others leave it but attempt to change the wording in a way to square the seeming contradiction.

But is there a contradiction? The number of chariots and horses, 100, remains consistent, as David cut the hamstrings of the other horses taken, and only kept 100 chariots.

To me it reads that David did the same with the horsemen themselves, decimating them and reserving 700 out of 7000, for the hundred chariots and horses he reserved.

Matthew Henry agrees with the King James reading and offers this explanation: "The horsemen are here said to be 700, but 1 Chronicles 18:4 they are said to be 7000. If they divided their horse by ten in a company, as it is probable they did, the captains and companies were 700, but the horsemen were 7000."

The fact that God inspired the retelling of much of these histories in two places written years apart, for our own knowledge and admonition, is a blessing. That they have been preserved for us is a providential miracle. Seeming discrepancies that can be explained by simple understanding, comparing the two accounts, should be understood to be a different view of the same event, not in error but giving an additional detail not given in the other. Or a clarification of a point God wished us to have.

That modern versions use these to cast doubt or to inject their own words is a mistake that comes from a lack of faith in the preservation of the word.

teachings.title: No Mandela effect in God's word
teachings.summary: Claims that the Bible was changed by a Mandela effect are blasphemy, because God's word is preserved and does not change.
teachings.text:
While I am on the subject of false doctrine coming from this chapter, those that claim this was changed;

*The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the bullock*..

That it "used to say the lamb lay down with the Lion! The Bible has been Mandela-effected!!" God's word is preserved by His power. It is an unchanging rock, settled in Heaven before the foundation of the world.

So no, you're wrong.

While it can be fun to have alternate theories of things of this world, when your schizo take leads to blasphemy, and profane babblings like this, take a step back and realize; sometimes you just are remembering an extra biblical account, or popular culture references.

God's word doesn't change.

teachings.title: Pure words preserved for ever
teachings.summary: God inspired His word and promised in Psalm 12 to preserve it pure for every generation, and the King James Bible is that purified, every-word English Bible without error, refined after six earlier English versions.
teachings.text:
*For the oppression of the poor, for the sighing of the needy, now will I arise, saith the LORD; I will set him in safety from him that puffeth at him.*

This is a promise from God Himself. These are His words.

**2 Peter 1:20–21**
*Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation. For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.*

The psalmist was moved by the holy Ghost to pen the words of the Lord. His promises are our sure foundation. His word settled forever in Heaven. Jesus is the Word made flesh. The promise fulfilled.

Faith cometh by hearing the word of God. Those that hear and do the things the Lord says are built upon a rock. We live by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God. All scripture is given by inspiration of God. It is the source of all our knowledge and understanding. His precepts give us understanding. We are told to meditate in His word day and night. To bind His words upon our heart. His words are powerful;

**Hebrews 1:1–3**
*God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds; Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high*

The word which we preach is the power to save men's souls to all who trust His word:

**Ephesians 1:12–14**
*That we should be to the praise of his glory, who first trusted in Christ. In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.*

And so, the preservation of God's word for all generations is a divine role. God supernaturally has revealed His word to man in sundry times and diverse manners, and He keeps His word pure.

*The words of the LORD are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times. Thou shalt keep them, O LORD, thou shalt preserve them from this generation for ever.*

If man needs every word of God to live, as much as bread, man needs access to every word He has given us.

The blessing of having a consolidated, complete, incorruptible source, an every-word Bible, cannot be overstated. The King James Bible is the every-word source, in English, without error.

The 6 earlier English attempts, like a refiner's fire. We have the purified silver of the Authorized version. We can know the Lord has preserved His word. We can trust and build upon that sure foundation.

teachings.title: Modern versions corrupt the promise of preservation
teachings.summary: The ESV changes Psalm 12:7 from God preserving His words to preserving men, casting doubt on preservation just as Satan asked, Yea, hath God said?
teachings.text:
Speaking of the sure word, preserved, modern versions change and corrupt this text. Rather than the promise to keep His words for all generations, they make it about preserving man;

The ESV: You, O Lord, will keep them; you will guard us[a] from this generation forever.

The footnotes cast doubt. The changes remove the Psalm's comparison of the vain words of the wicked with certainty of God's word of promise.

The Lord promises to hear the sighing of the needy, and to arise to set them that call upon Him in safety. It is that promise that is preserved. And must be, or God is a liar.

The first thing modern versions do is create doubt and deny the preservation of the inspired word. Just as Satan tempted Eve in the garden, asking "Yea, hath God said?"

*The wicked walk on every side, when the vilest men are exalted.*

But the hope is in the help of the Lord, promised to us before the foundation of the world.

teachings.title: The Authorized English loses nothing
teachings.summary: The Hebrew acrostic form may be lost in translation, but the King James loses nothing of the power and truth of God's word.
teachings.text:
In the original Hebrew, David used the format of an "alphabetic acrostic psalm," where stanzas begin with consecutive letters, to act as an mnemonic device, and form of poetry, that David uses multiple times in Psalms.

This stylized form of writing is "lost" in translation, some textual critics may say, but the strained gnat of it all makes them miss the power of what we have in English.

The repeated calls to trust the Lord, seek forgiveness, humbly petition and wait with patience is all beautifully expressed in Psalm 25 as we read it here. The prose of the Authorized English loses nothing to the power of God's word.

So, while it is interesting to note the format, and discuss the ways it was used (here, imperfectly with missing and skipped letters) it isn't necessary for the truth to prick our hearts and give us comfort.

teachings.title: Building on the rock of God's word
teachings.theme: Every word of God is pure
teachings.summary: Biblical fundamentalism, preaching the whole unchanging word, is the only safeguard, which is why it has been attacked from every direction for two centuries.
teachings.text:
This is why biblical fundamentalism is so important. It is the only safeguard we have. Preaching the whole of the word, Genesis and Judges 19, Leviticus, Deuteronomy, teaching the reprobate doctrine, replacement theology and the nature of Jews as antichrists, liars, contrary to all men, and the synagogue of Satan.

For 200 years in America they attacked biblical fundamentalism from every direction, whether it was dispensationalism, rationalism, evolution, the development of judeo-christian nonsense, the importation of massive numbers of false religions like Catholicism, promotion of new age, atheism and paganism, placing politics above God, and of course the sodomite LGBT agenda.

Once you have no real, solid, unchanging foundation for what you believe it becomes difficult to argue against critics, maintain standards, etc.

Basing your faith on the unchanging and preserved word of God is building on rock. Everything else is sand.

teachings.title: Easter in Acts 12:4 is not pagan
teachings.theme: Every word of God is pure
teachings.summary: The KJV's Easter in Acts 12:4 is a deliberate English name for the resurrection feast meaning dawn, not a pagan holiday or a word from Ishtar.
teachings.text:
The translators calling this Passover mentioned in Acts 12 "Easter" in the KJV has caused confusion and consternation for many.

 Some falsely teach that KJV uses “Easter” at Acts 12:4 to indicate some pagan holiday celebration by Herod. Not only was the translation of the same word used as Passover elsewhere, the 1611 version contained a page for finding the date of Easter based on lunar days that specifically called that Sunday celebration of Jesus' resurrection 'Easter.'

Another misconception is that the word shares an etymology with pagan goddess Ishtar or Astarte, a myth propagated in the 1800s:

"Astarte is “עשׁתּרות (ashtarot)” in Hebrew.  This name is derived from the word “עשׁתּרה (‛ashterâh)” which means “increase” or “flock” (Brown-Driver-Briggs’ Hebrew Definitions).  “עשׁתּרה (‛ashterâh)” is translated as “flocks” four times in the KJV.  Hence, the name “Astarte” or “Ishtar” is a Semitic word related to animal fertility.

The etymology of “Easter” on the other hand has nothing to do with “flocks” or animal fertility.  “Easter” (“Ostern” in German) is a Germanic word derived from the word “east” (“Ost” in German).  Today, “east” refers to the direction from which the sun rises.  The direction of east goes by that name because the Saxon word “east” meant “dawn”, “sunrise” or “morning.”'

“Easter” means “dawn”
The Old English word for the month of April was “Eosturmonað” coming from Old Germanic, Ōstar-mānod.

While there may have been Anglo-Saxon pagans naming their spring goddess after the older, Germanic terms, the name of the month and its meaning of Eastern/dawn predates them.

So, the origins come from the treatment of early Germanic/Anglo-Saxon Christians naming the day as the the “dawn” par excellence. The supreme dawn of the resurrection of Christ.

And the translators giving name to the holy day that was 'pascha' or Passover, now being Easter, post resurrection is deliberate, and has nothing to do with paganism.

teachings.title: Man shall not live by bread alone
teachings.theme: Every word of God is pure
teachings.summary: Satan tempts us as he did Eve and Christ by twisting scripture to justify the flesh, and Jesus shows we overcome him and live by every word of God.
teachings.text:
Following Jesus' baptism and the announcement of the Father that this was His Son in Whom He was well pleased and the anointing by the Holy Ghost, Jesus went into the wilderness to fast. Knowing hunger, being in the flesh, He was tested and tried of all things and yet sinless.

When Satan came and likewise tempted Him with rewards of the flesh, twisting scripture to do it, Jesus cites the word to both rebuke the devil and keep Himself pure.

This is how Satan attacks us all. He wanders the earth like a ravening lion, seeking who he can devour. He is before God the Father accusing believers, day and night. He gets us to give in to lusts of the flesh, and if possible, gets us to justify it as God's will by twisting His word. Same as with Eve in the garden. Same as with the Son of God in the wilderness.

And unlike Eve, Jesus rebuke sends the devil packing, defeated and angels are sent to minister to Christ.

Matthew then tells the story of the beginning of Jesus' ministry, the recruitment of some of the apostles from Galilee, having gone there to avoid Judea after the arrest of John the Baptist.

The willingness of the apostles to leave father, home, job, everything to follow Christ is an example to all believers and seekers. As we know from Gospel of John, they were seeking the Messiah of the prophets already, and heard their master's voice when He called. Knowing the scriptures, they knew His word, and the promise and so, when called heard His voice.

This is why we are reminded that scripture said that man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God. It's Jesus' first lesson to us. We live by His word.

teachings.title: Paul's apostleship and the one voice of scripture
teachings.theme: Every word of God is pure
teachings.summary: God repeatedly affirmed Paul's apostleship because heretics attack his epistles, yet all 66 books are one word with one voice, and repeated doctrines like the pastoral epistles are given for emphasis.
teachings.text:
Paul, opens as he often does, professing he is a servant of God, and an Apostle, as evidenced by those who have believed his preaching unto salvation. His bona fides being those who believe. They having hope of eternal life, which God who cannot lie, promised before the world began, made manifest by the preaching of believers called to ministry of the Gospel. The preaching of this good news, which was commanded of Paul by Jesus Himself. The faith of those who received it of him bearing record. The fruit he has produced.

This comes up often in Acts, and in most of his letters, and it's important to understand why God chose to repeatedly make this point, that Paul was His Apostle, *born out of due time.*

There is heresy out there calling in to question Paul's authority, and casting doubt on his writings and doctrines, which make up a bulk of the NT books. Doubt that wicked men seek to cast to keep those ignorant of the truth from ever considering the epistles as scripture, not understanding that there is a perfect consistency between the inspired words of the prophets, patriarchs, Christ Jesus and His Apostles. Let alone considering the need of the clarity of doctrine regarding the implications of the common faith, of eternal life, by Grace. The mystery being revealed by the manifestation of Jesus in the flesh, His death, burial and His resurrection. Of how we are to partake in the promise, and having been adopted by God into His Kingdom, what then? What's next, having been saved?

And so, thank God, He sought to give us the epistles, that we may be more perfect in our understanding. Just as He gave us the prophets, that we could be made meet for repentance, and the Gospels so we may know what we are to turn towards, we are given the Acts and letters of the apostles so we may know what we should do once we have turned toward God. And Revelation of Jesus Christ, that we may know what is to come.

It is all one word, one testimony, one book made up of 66 smaller books, written over thousands of years, but with one voice, the inspiration of God, through the Spirit, testifying of the Son.

Sometimes people lose sight of this. People who having believed the word, and should know better, as they have the same Spirit testifying to its power, within them.

It is never so important to keep this in mind as when reading the Pastoral Epistles, 1st and 2nd Timothy, which we covered this past few weeks, and Titus today.

At issue is the original organization of local churches. Of the offices and expectations, and the doctrines that should be preserved and taught among the congregations.

Even supposed Christian denominations, especially those that claim an "Apostolic Tradition," will cast doubt on the epistles, denying Paul's authority by countermanding his doctrines, ignoring them, or claiming there were oral tradition that differs significantly from the whole body of scripture that contradicts their own edicts.

There's a saying in studying scripture, that nothing in God's word is coincidental, incidental or accidental. And a maxim that if God repeats something, it is for emphasis and our edification. That it's important for us to get it. Much of scripture is terse, and brief and pithy. Giving exactly enough to convey the message intended. So, when God repeats the same lesson, we should listen.

The Pastoral Epistles are an excellent example of this. One cannot say "Well, Paul was just telling Timothy this, we can't claim it's in all cases..." when he repeats the same doctrines to Titus. Just as Jude and Peter wrote nearly identical messages to the churches, just as we have four Gospel accounts. God's perfect judgement calls for multiple witness to establish truth, and He provides the same for us that we may believe Him, and those He sent.

teachings.title: Yea, hath God said? Satan's oldest trick
teachings.theme: Every word of God is pure
teachings.summary: Satan's first tactic was casting doubt on God's word, the same strategy behind modern Bible versions, footnotes and scholars who undermine scripture.
teachings.text:
Now, what was the command of God? **Genesis 2**:16-17;

*And the Lord God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat: But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.*

And we note this was given Adam, before Eve was. And told to Eve by Adam. Which is how God's word is given each of us. Spoken of the LORD God, by faith passed down to others, by faith received and believed. And it is that faith in the received word of God that Satan, more subtle than any beast, preys on, when as the serpent he comes to tempt Eve;

*And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?*
