"Ye, hath God said?" This is Satan's oldest trick. Casting doubt upon God's word to get us to sin. This is the reason for false Bible versions. This is the way of false prophets. Making us doubt that God's word is pure and right.

"Many of the earliest manuscripts leave this passage out...this verse is not found in earlier manuscripts...the Greek here could actually mean this instead. Do you even know Hebrew?" Footnotes. Margin notes. "Study Bibles." "You need a seminary graduate with a doctorate in Divinity to understand the Bible!" "God of the OT is angry, but Jesus is love!" "That was written to people of *that* time, not to us!"

Fill in your own example of "Yea, hath God said..?" here.

*And the woman said unto the serpent, We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden: But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.*

*And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die: For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.*

The serpent misquotes and questions, Eve knows the truth of the word and corrects him. Then Satan incredulously casts more doubt.

And this doubt, we see work in Eve, sparking the curiosity and wonder and reason, gifts of God that make us like unto Him, but now, under our will and doubts sown by Satan, used to choose sin.

And so she *saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise*, and so curious and doubting, covetous of the wisdom of God, Eve was beguiled into sin, and ate of the tree.

And Adam? Eve *gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.*

There's no subtlety, no casting of doubt. No tricks of the serpent. His wife sinned and he readily joined in immediately. Of his own free will.

Many such cases. Misery loves company and the sin of those around us, like the little leaven that leavens the whole lump, it spreads.

teachings.title: The flood is true because the Bible says so
teachings.theme: Every word of God is pure
teachings.summary: The global flood is true because God's word says so, and believers should answer scoffers with meekness and the faith of Noah.
teachings.text:
The Bible says that God's judgment came upon the wicked and the scoffers, and the corrupt earth tainted with the blood of violence and sin, and just Noah was saved, with his sons and their wives, along with the animals of the earth. That all flesh died otherwise in a global flood, waters pouring in from the skies like through open windows, up from the deep like a fountain, and covered the earth for 150 days. This is true.

There are archeologies and secular histories that all confirm a global flood, relegated to 'myth' status but wondered about by natural men, seeking to confirm the story by natural means.

We could go into the fossils of sealife found on top of Everest, or deposits of salt in high plateaus. The deluge changing the face of the earth in grand canyons and fiords and river beds. The common DNA, traced to the time of Noah. Etc.

But the Bible says it's true, and that's enough.

Scoffers laugh at the idea of Biblical Fundamentalism, and some believers take it personally and are embarrassed by the word of God, even as the science of man comes around to confirming the accounts of scripture.

We shouldn't be moved but rather, those scoffers should be embarrassed by themselves and their own foolish hearts. The Bible tells us how we should act when facing them, and puts their fate in perspective for us;

**1 Peter 3**

*And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good? But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled; But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ. For it is better, if the will of God be so, that ye suffer for well doing, than for evil doing.*

*For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit: By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison; Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water. The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ.*

Jesus was triumphantly shown in Hell before those that didn't believe, preaching His glory, leaving captivity captive.

Noah and his family were given physical salvation as the scoffers and unbelievers who mocked God were swallowed up in the flood.

**2 Peter 2**
*For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment; And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly; And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly; And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;) The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished:*

We are called to have the faith of Noah, who, having the grace of God extended to him, and faith in the Christ to come, believed God's promise of salvation. Building the ark, diligently and meekly, obeying the Lord. Like Lot, vexed by the filthy, sinful fallen man around him. Yet Noah stayed true, and God delivered him and  destroyed the wicked, just as He will in the great day of the Lord.

teachings.title: Man lives by every word of God
teachings.theme: Every word of God is pure
teachings.summary: All scripture is given by inspiration and is the only and final authority, sufficient for doctrine, as Jesus showed against Satan in the desert.
teachings.text:
I will continue the rest of the chapter later. The chapters in Luke are long and cover multiple stories of Christ.

We will see later in this chapter that Jesus again quotes scripture to the people and we should note that already in the past 3 chapters, and all through the book, the scriptures are referenced constantly. The law and Psalms and words of the prophets.

Because, *All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.*

Man lives *by every word of God.*

Biblical fundamentalism. That God's word is the only and final authority. All we need for doctrine that we may be perfect, whole, complete.

It was good enough for Jesus in the desert against Satan. It is good enough for us today who follow Him.

teachings.title: One consistent voice in all of scripture
teachings.theme: Every word of God is pure
teachings.summary: He notes that Moses, the prophets, the apostles and Christ all speak with one clear voice because all scripture is given by the same Spirit, not the works of men.
teachings.text:
The remaining parts of the chapter are fairly straightforward establishing sanctuary cities on the east side of the Jordan in the lands given to the Rubenites, Gadites and Manasseh, which decided they'd be happy with the fertile plains for their cattle, just short of the promised land. These cities established for those that accidentally kill someone else, that they could flee to and be given refuge, as dictated in Leviticus.

There are a few more chapters before we get into the meat of the retelling of the law. As we go through however, Note that there is a consistent voice in scripture. Whether it is Moses, the prophets, the apostles... Christ Himself, all of it has a consistent and clear voice. Reading **Deuteronomy 4** and then going to read **Galatians** for this study, I was struck so hard by how consistent the word of God is. All given by the same Spirit. Not a collection of the works of men, but the word of an eternal and living God.

teachings.title: Add not to the word nor diminish
teachings.theme: Every word of God is pure
teachings.summary: He teaches that the word of God is the only authority, given plainly and preserved so even a babe in Christ can understand it, unlike mystery religions and gnosticism.
teachings.text:
*What thing soever I command you, observe to do it: thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it.*

And, again we see the doctrine of fundamentalism, that the word of God is the only authority we follow, and that those who add to or take away from the word of God are wicked. The word of God is given in clear, easy to understand verses. Holy men speaking in times past through the Spirit. Recorded in the Bible for us today. Preserved for all time. The inspired word of God. The Father gives us His will, and repeats it over and over that we get the point. Even here, in this chapter, there is redundancy. Deuteronomy itself is a second telling of the same law. God gives us examples of those who follow Him and are blessed. Who disobey and are cursed. All of creation as parables that we may understand. The Spirit to bring us to understanding, repentance towards belief. God wants us to know Him and His will for our lives.

It is the opposite of mystery religions and gnosticism. All of the information is given up front and the means to understand provided even the lowliest babe in Christ. We just have to read it for ourselves.

As the Lord God says to Daniel, *But I will shew thee that which is noted in the scripture of truth*... As He says in Isaiah, *Come now, and let us reason together, saith the Lord: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.*

*God is not the author of confusion.*

teachings.title: Evil in the KJV does not mean sin
teachings.theme: Every word of God is pure
teachings.summary: The KJV saying God does evil means calamity, not sin, as Webster's and Jonah 3 show, and church fathers cannot contradict God's preserved word.
teachings.text:
"The King James Bible translates God saying He does 'evil,' and muh church fathers said God doesn't do evil, so I debunked KJV Onlyism!"

"Evil" doesn't mean sin. According to Webster's and its use in the Bible, 'Evil' is defined as *Unfortunate; unhappy; producing sorrow, distress, injury or calamity; as evil tidings; evil arrows; evil days.*

E'VIL, *is natural or moral. Natural evil is any thing which produces pain, distress, loss or calamity, or which in any way disturbs the peace, impairs the happiness, or destroys the perfection of natural beings.Moral evil is any deviation of a moral agent from the rules of conduct prescribed to him by God, or by legitimate human authority; or it is any violation of the plain principles of justice and rectitude.*

**Jonah 3:5-10**
*And Jonah began to enter into the city a day's journey, and he cried, and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown. So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them. For word came unto the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, and he laid his robe from him, and covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes. And he caused it to be proclaimed and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water: But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily unto God: yea, let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands Who can tell if God will turn and repent, and turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not? And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.*

Here is evil used both ways, and clearly defined (along with repent being a change of mind).

"Church fathers" aren't a source that can contradict the word of God, and a natural man's ignorance as to the meaning of a word isn't an argument against His preserved word.

teachings.title: Tekton and carpenter, no contradiction
teachings.theme: Every word of God is pure
teachings.summary: Tekton and carpenter both mean a skilled builder, so there is no contradiction, and Christ the builder framed the world.
teachings.text:
Maybe...just hear me out...maybe they mean the same thing. Both "tektōn" (Greek) and "carpenter" describe skilled craftsmen who contribute to building buildings and structures, particularly but not exclusively through woodworking. In the context of **Mark 6:3,** both terms suggest Jesus was involved in skilled construction-related work, including being a framer, designing and building the structural elements of buildings, e.g., wooden beams, framing, roofs, etc...as well as the stonework and the like.

Knowing that He framed the world, that He is the corner stone, the right angle, the foundation...all these construction terms and concepts, brings the spiritual to life.

So there is no contradiction.

I thank God His word was settled in Heaven before the framing of the world, amen.

teachings.title: Every word out of His mouth
teachings.theme: Every word of God is pure
teachings.summary: Since wisdom proceeds from the mouth of God and man lives by every word of God, we need a Bible that keeps every word, which in English is only the King James Bible.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 2** continues the instruction on Wisdom, and The importance of accepting her as the truth of God. That Spirit of truth that we as Christians are given, so long as we receive it, walking in the Spirit, walking in God's word.

We go to church to hear the word preached (faith cometh by hearing), as we incline our ear unto wisdom. Not being, as many are described in scripture, dull of hearing. We should rather be ready to hear and to keep it in our hearts, as doers of the word.

We should seek the wisdom of God as it were silver, a treasure. More valuable than riches is the wisdom of God's commandments.

**Matthew 7:24** *Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock*

A wise man cries for knowledge, and lifts up their voice for understanding. Asking God for His wisdom, like Solomon did. Ask and it shall be given you. Seek it and ye shall find. And with knowledge, understanding, and in doing what God says, we grow in faith.

**Hebrews 11:6** *But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.*

*The Lord giveth wisdom.* Out of His mouth:

**Matthew 4:4** *But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.*

If wisdom proceeds out of the mouth of God, and we live by every word of God, and all scripture is given, inspired by God, written by holy men of God who spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost, we need to have a Bible that conveys all of them. That we may be perfect, complete and throughly furnished having everything we need. In English, this is found only in the authorized version of the King James Bible, the perfect and preserved word of God.

teachings.title: Every word of God is pure
teachings.theme: Every word of God is pure
teachings.summary: Because every word of God is pure and must not be added to or taken from, we need an every-word Bible, which God has preserved in English in the Authorized Version.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 30** introduces the "sayings of Agur," who, some argue, is not Solomon, but possibly the sayings of a Gentile wiseman, under the influence of the Spirit. However, Jewish tradition views this as a pseudonym for King Solomon, describing him as one who "gathered" or collected wisdom.

Jakeh, means pious and faithfully religious. It may be a title, rather than a name.

The passage is addressed to Ithiel and Ucal, possibly students or symbolic names meaning "God with me" and "I am strong," respectively.

These wise sayings were included in the scripture that Hezekiah's scribes compiled at the righteous King's request.

The humble self-deprecation of the introduction in v2-3 ironically demonstrates this man's wisdom. Admission that as a brutish, or generally stupid man, with no training or knowledge, before dropping insightful and prophetic oracles, is a key to wisdom. Humility and willingness to grasp that even the smartest man doesn't know all the ways of God, is itself wise.

Immediately, we are given an understanding of God and prophetic mention of Jesus, that also serves as a reminder of the limitations man has in understanding God.

Asking rhetorically, Who it is that has done these things? What is His name? We know it is the Lord. What is His Son's name? We know it is Jesus. But the glass darkly that they saw through pointed only at the Son, not the name. Further revelation has given us the only name under Heaven by which a man may be saved.

Regardless of the identity of the human author, the Spirit is showing us that even in the day of Solomon, and the Kings of Judah, God's Christ was known and believed on.

v5-6 give the inspired case for Biblical fundamentalism. Every word of God is pure.

**2 Peter 1:19-21**
*We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts: Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation. For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.*

And if every word of God is pure, we need an "every word" Bible. We are blessed that we have one, in the Authorized version, in English. Preserved by God unto all generations.

*God is a shield unto them that out their trust in Him* is the promise of the gospel. The same yesterday, today and forever.

And the curse against changing His word, adding to it, bringing false gospels, remains consistent;

*Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar*.

Be it Satan, in the beginning, asking Eve "Yea, hath God said" in **Genesis 3:1,** or modern churches claiming Christ while adding to and perverting the word to deceive. The wrath of God against those that corrupt His pure word.

**Deuteronomy 4:2**
*Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it, that ye may keep the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you.*

**Revelation 22:18-19**
*For I testify unto every man that heareth the words of the prophecy of this book, If any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book: And if any man shall take away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part out of the book of life, and out of the holy city, and from the things which are written in this book.*

The sure knowledge that we can trust the word of God is a foundation which we can build a strong fortress upon.

**Matthew 7:24-25**
*Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.*

teachings.title: 2 Thessalonians 2:15 does not overturn scripture
teachings.summary: Holding the traditions Paul taught cannot mean secret teachings contradicting scripture, and heretics cherry-pick that verse against God's complete word.
teachings.text:
2 Thessalonians 2 doesn't "refute Sola scripta," (a term I hate.. It's just the Bible is the complete word of God).

Up front, any argument made that ignores the clear teachings of scripture, OT and NT, that scripture is inspired, preserved and complete "whole word of God," and directly from Jesus against holding to extra-scriptural traditions over scripture itself, is already proven wrong.

**Proverbs 30:6**
 *Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.*

Many such a cases.

People looking to defend heresy won't ever address the multiple instances of clear scripture that contradicts them, or explain with equally clear scripture how the first scripture is wrong.

What they do is cherry pick a single verse, out of context that if presented to unsaved people, ignorant of the Bible can maybe confuse them enough to see it their way.

2 Thessalonians 2:15 is a perfect example of this. Ignoring the context of the epistle, and specifically the chapter it's pulled from, they will argue this:

*Therefore, brethren, stand fast, and hold the traditions which ye have been taught, whether by word, or our epistle.*

..trumps all scripture, and allows contrary teachings to scripture to supercede scripture.

One, it's a foolish argument even taken as is. Paul would never tell Thessalonians to "stand fast" to a tradition that was preached to them in person, if it contradicts the word and epistles he just told them to hold to. That is absurd. "Wink wink, you know that secret stuff we told you but didn't write down? Yeah that says it's ok to worship idols and baptized babies and have a universal church controlled by men? Vain repetitive prayers? Works to be saved? Yeah hold on to that." It's not even a rational argument using the logic of men. Especially given the scriptures and epistles directly contradict the vain traditions of men being defended. This "proof text" alone contradicts the point being argued.

But taken in its context, it isn't even saying what is being alleged by the heretics.

teachings.title: The traditions were end-times teaching from scripture
teachings.summary: In context, the traditions of 2 Thessalonians 2 were Paul's scriptural teaching on Christ's coming, not hidden doctrines.
teachings.text:
Paul is writing to the independent NT church in Thessalonica with a specific message regarding a specific topic; End times prophecy.

We don't have to guess at what mystery doctrines were being given by these "traditions" given the church by word and epistle. Paul tells us in the second verse:

*That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand.*

Judaizers and heretics, even in these first days of NT Christianity, were spreading lies and false doctrine that contradicted the scriptures. Paul is writing to reassure them and warn against it:

*Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except.*.. And he lists the order of events regarding the resurrection and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Paul says "*Remember ye not, that, when I was yet with you, I told you these things?"* Reminding them of the in-person teaching he gave regarding this specific topic. Teachings that came from the Holy Ghost, through the gospel accounts of Christ's ministry and OT scriptures.

There were men trying to deceive them regarding the resurrection and return. He wrote to remind them of what was taught to them, giving us 2000yrs later the same instruction on the same doctrine.

*Therefore, brethren, stand fast, and hold the traditions which ye have been taught, whether by word, or our epistle.* Amen! Yes. Standfast whether you learned this Biblical doctrine on the rapture and day of the Lord through preaching by an Apostle or evangelist gifted by the Holy Ghost, taken from scripture and the words of Christ, or by epistles. Amen!

teachings.title: The pattern of heretical proof texts
teachings.summary: Heretics strip verses of context, ignore contradicting scripture and appeal to church fathers, and God sends strong delusion to those who love not the truth.
teachings.text:
All heretical doctrines and apologetics follow this pattern of stripping scripture of meaning, adding irrational argument to it, and ignoring the scriptures that contradicts their heresy. Just as I said.

What they will never do it post an entire chapter or book that surrounds their "proof text," and they won't ever attempt to square the differences with other scripture, just offer non sequitur citation and act as though it's an argument.

They may make an appeal to some 5th century "church fathers," but they won't ever use the whole word of God to defend their position. In fact, being unsaved and unable to understand scripture when shown, they act like robots in Westworld being shown a photo of modernity, "I don't see anything."

As Paul writes in **2 Thessalonians 2**, regarding Satan fooling unsaved people with false Gospels and doctrines:

*And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved. And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.*

teachings.title: Making the word of none effect by tradition
teachings.summary: Jesus in Mark 7 condemned traditions that make God's word of none effect, so any tradition of man contradicting scripture is heresy.
teachings.text:
Key points of Jesus preaching in Mark 7:

*For laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men, as the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things ye do...And he said unto them, Full well ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your own tradition...Making the word of God of none effect through your tradition, which ye have delivered: and many such like things do ye.*

Making the word of God, which is scripture, *of none effect through your tradition*.

He uses an example of the Jews tradition, allowing a son to dishonor their parents by declaring their wealth "Corban," or a gift to the temple while keeping and using the wealth for themselves. But this applies to ANY extra-scriptural doctrines and traditions that contradicts the word of God. Making God's word to none effect by their traditions.

There is your Biblical "Sola scripta" doctrine (cringe latin term for biblical fundamentalism) straight from Jesus Christ Himself.

Any tradition of man that contradicts scripture is heresy. Period.

teachings.title: Paul reasoned out of the scriptures
teachings.summary: Acts 17 shows the apostles preached from the scriptures and the Bereans checked them by scripture, so there were no secret oral traditions contrary to the word.
teachings.text:
The Book of Acts shows that the Apostles and those given the gift of the Holy Ghost, evangelists, who went out to preach the word of God and the Gospel, the Good news of Christ, taught the doctrine of Christ from scripture.

**Acts 17** details this well:

*Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews:*

*2 And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures,*

*3 Opening and alleging, that Christ must needs have suffered, and risen again from the dead; and that this Jesus, whom I preach unto you, is Christ.*

*4 And some of them believed, and consorted with Paul and Silas; and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few.*

*5 But the Jews which believed not, moved with envy, took unto them certain lewd fellows of the baser sort, and gathered a company, and set all the city on an uproar, and assaulted the house of Jason, and sought to bring them out to the people.*

*6 And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brethren unto the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also;*

*7 Whom Jason hath received: and these all do contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, one Jesus.*

*8 And they troubled the people and the rulers of the city, when they heard these things.*

*9 And when they had taken security of Jason, and of the other, they let them go.*

*10 And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night unto Berea: who coming thither went into the synagogue of the Jews.*

*11 These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.*

*12 Therefore many of them believed; also of honourable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few.*

*13 But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was preached of Paul at Berea, they came thither also, and stirred up the people.*

*14 And then immediately the brethren sent away Paul to go as it were to the sea: but Silas and Timotheus abode there still.*

*15 And they that conducted Paul brought him unto Athens: and receiving a commandment unto Silas and Timotheus for to come to him with all speed, they departed.*

*16 Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry.*

*17 Therefore disputed he in the synagogue with the Jews, and with the devout persons, and in the market daily with them that met with him.*

People who don't read the Bible and can't understand it if they do, will often make sweeping claims that their heretical ideas and false doctrines must be true based on some twisted logic of man. Claims that simply knowing the Bible easily refute.

They claim because the Gospel was preached orally that there were secret traditions given that were in conflict with clear teaching from scripture, when in fact what was preached was from scripture. Jesus is the fufilment of the OT. The Law. The promise to Abraham. And scripture is how we know this is true. Just as Paul and the apostles used scripture to convert the Thessalonians here in Acts 17, and just as he wrote to them in epistles to stand fast to the teachings from scripture that he gave them in person in 2 Thessalonians 2.

He gave them no instruction or tradition that contradicted scripture or else how would they search *the scriptures daily, whether those things were so?*

The proof text Catholics use to denigrate the word of God and justify their damnable heresies behind "tradition," is undone by simply reading the word.

*Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.*

teachings.title: Paul received no gospel from man
teachings.summary: Paul received his gospel by revelation, not from men's traditions, and anyone preaching another gospel of works is accursed.
teachings.text:
Notice, Paul writing to the Galatians in the Spirit, God inspired scripture, says this TWICE. For emphasis.

And what was it he preached to the Galatians?

*For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ. But I certify you, brethren, that the gospel which was preached of me is not after man. For I neither received it of man, neither was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ.*

 *For ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews' religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it:*

*And profited in the Jews' religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers. But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mother's womb, and called me by his grace, To reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the heathen; immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood: Neither went I up to Jerusalem to them which were apostles before me; but I went into Arabia, and returned again unto Damascus. Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen days.But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord's brother.*

*Now the things which I write unto you, behold, before God, I lie not. Afterwards I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia; And was unknown by face unto the churches of Judaea which were in Christ: But they had heard only, That he which persecuted us in times past now preacheth the faith which once he destroyed. And they glorified God in me.*

Don't miss this, Paul makes it emphatically clear he didn't learn any secret traditions of man from any Apostles. He wasn't told what to say by anyone else. He, knowing the scriptures and having by the grace of God the opportunity for salvation in Jesus, was given all to preach to the heathen.

He explains how, after 14 years the issue of Judaizers and the circumcision brought him to go to Jerusalem and talk to the local church there, run by James BTW, and they agreed to send letters out denouncing the judaizers adding works to salvation, and affirming the Gospel:

*Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.*

This is the Gospel. And ANY MAN bringing any other Gospel, especially of works and rites for salvation, IS ACCURSED.

teachings.title: The red letters are the scriptures
teachings.summary: Saying we should focus only on the red letters is a natural man's error, since Jesus is the Word and His sayings are the fulfilment of all scripture and its doctrine.
teachings.text:
I feel weird about trying to give a study of what Jesus is saying here, when His words are so plain and easily understood, His parables in this passage aren't dark sayings, He is desperately trying to impart these things to His disciples before His eventual crucifixion. It's a ticking clock we see Jesus is all too aware of.

*But I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how am I straitened till it be accomplished!*

Straitened, meaning constrained to a narrow path, Jesus laments showing frustration at this hypocritical generation. That they don't see it all clearly, and the press of time is all too real for Him that was before time, now made in corruptible flesh that He may deliver man.

Some people say things like "we need to just focus on the red letters, and not worry so much about other doctrines and disputes over scripture!" But that's a natural man misunderstanding; the red letters ARE the scriptures, Jesus is the Word of God. His preaching and parables are the fulfilment of the law, the doctrines of God. They aren't isolated or contradictions. I mention this because, in my experience, people who say that don't actually read the red letters. It's a cope to not have to deal with the meaning and implications of the Bible. To really study the word and understand the fundamentalism Jesus is preaching.

By the same token, we can be lost in the weeds of doctrine at times. It is a good thing to really consider the words of Jesus, and apply them to our lives. Praying on them that we can see the revealed will of God.

Jesus lived in the flesh a short while, His earthly ministry only 3 and a half years, the Gospels our only record of His teachings, teachings He knew He had so little time to convey. Go back and really read and consider the chapter, in that light. Spend time with the words of Jesus, it will change you. Amen

teachings.title: Written aforetime for our learning
teachings.summary: Romans 15:4 shows that scripture is the means by which we learn God's doctrine and the source of our hope, meant to make believers likeminded.
teachings.text:
*For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.*

This is another proof text for scripture being the means by which we learn the doctrines of God. God's word is powerful and where our hope comes from, the object of our faith. The truth of God's word.

Paul's prayer is that the patience and consolation of the Gospel, taught in scriptures, the understanding of the implications of our shared faith and common salvation, would bring the churches in Rome, and the thousands of churches that have read Romans, to be likeminded regarding these things, that they may in one accord glorify God. That they may receive each other and the brethren in peace and patience and love, the way Jesus received us to the glory of God. To reveal the righteousness of God to the nations through our salvation.

teachings.title: What is written is sufficient
teachings.summary: Against a Catholic claim from John 20-21 of unwritten oral doctrines, he shows those verses speak of signs and say the written word is sufficient to believe and have life.
teachings.text:
Next he cites **John 20:30** and **John 21:25** claiming they teach that there are unwritten doctrines only known by oral tradition. Let's look at it in context;

**John 20:29-31**
*Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed. And many other signs truly did Jesus in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book: But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.*

**John 21:24-25**
*This is the disciple which testifieth of these things, and wrote these things: and we know that his testimony is true. And there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which, if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written. Amen.*

These clearly are acts of Jesus, miracles and signs, not doctrines. But what does the Apostle John tell us? That what is written is sufficient to believe on Jesus Christ, the Son of God, and by believing, have life through His name.

If there were need of other records of the signs performed by Jesus, which are so many the world couldn't contain the books required to record them, in order to give us the knowledge to be saved, John wouldn't be able to truthfully write that what was given as testimony was enough.

teachings.title: More blessed to give: not oral tradition
teachings.summary: He answers the Catholic use of Acts 20:35 by showing Christ taught the same in Luke 6:38, so the written word, not tradition, preserves His teaching.
teachings.text:
Next is the claim that **Acts 20:35** says that Jesus' had testimony not found in the gospels. (They use their weird Latin abbreviation for Jesus here, INH). But is that what it says?

*I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.*

They will say "see? That exact quote doesn't appear in the gospels!"

But does the idea contained in it?

**Luke 6:38**
*Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.*

So Jesus taught that it is more blessed to give, that by doing so, by the same measure it will be given back to you.

When Paul, in the Spirit is speaking to the church at Ephesus, the four Gospel accounts had not yet been written. He's not quoting the Gospels, but Christ, Who taught that the Spirit will bring to remembrance all that He said. Luke, in the Spirit is recording it.

And so it is God's intended word, written for our benefit, inspired and preserved, even if it is a paraphrase of a doctrine that was taught by Christ or a direct quote given by the Spirit of that same teaching.

It's a foolish argument to claim that since it is recorded this way here, it isn't what was taught and only available by tradition, when up to this point in Acts, all the words of Christ had been given by preaching.

teachings.title: The tradition Paul gave is written
teachings.summary: He shows Paul's tradition in 2 Thessalonians 3 is written in the epistle and that 2 Peter 1 says scripture came by the Holy Ghost, the opposite of Catholic claims.
teachings.text:
Quickly let me wrap this up.

**2 Thessalonians 3:6**
*Now we command you, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye withdraw yourselves from every brother that walketh disorderly, and not after the tradition which he received of us.*

Again, Paul writes what that tradition is.

*For yourselves know how ye ought to follow us: for we behaved not ourselves disorderly among you; Neither did we eat any man's bread for nought; but wrought with labour and travail night and day, that we might not be chargeable to any of you: Not because we have not power, but to make ourselves an ensample unto you to follow us. For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not work, neither should he eat.*
*For we hear that there are some which walk among you disorderly, working not at all, but are busybodies. Now them that are such we command and exhort by our Lord Jesus Christ, that with quietness they work, and eat their own bread. But ye, brethren, be not weary in well doing. And if any man obey not our word by this epistle, note that man, and have no company with him, that he may be ashamed. Yet count him not as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.*

**Acts 8:31** is referring to giving the Gospel which as we know has to come from a saved Christian using the word of God.

And finally, **2 Peter 1:19-21**
*We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts:*
*Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation. For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.*

Peter is directly stating that scripture comes from the inspiration of the Holy Ghost. Not made up by men, not just given by their own imagination. That we can count on it even more than what Peter witnessed with his own eyes and heard with his own ears on the mount of transfiguration, when God spoke from the clouds.

He's literally saying the opposite of what the Catholic Church is trying to rationalize.

teachings.title: The word of the Lord was precious
teachings.summary: As in Samuel's day there is no open vision now, but we have God's full revelation in His word and need no private interpretation, so the word should be kept precious.
teachings.text:
*And the word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no open vision.*

Samuel, still a child, is serving Eli at the Tabernacle, in service to the Lord. And we are told that the word of the Lord was precious, because there were no open visions. God wasn't speaking to man. Prophets were few and far between, perhaps the man of God who spoke the curses to Eli in the previous chapter had the last vision. All that remained was God's established word.

We are currently in the same state; there is no open vision, and so the word of the Lord should be kept precious.

We have His full revelation, we have no need for anything of private interpretation. We should then seek to know the word, that we know His will.

But in Samuel's day the full revelation was still over a millennia away. And so when the Lord calls the boy, and Eli realizes what's going on, he instructs his young apprentice to answer, *Speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth.*

And when the Lord came, and stood and called out to Samuel, the boy answered as he was told.

I believe that this is Christ Jesus speaking to Him. The Lord God in the flesh, as He appeared throughout the Old Testament, because the Bible says He stood before Samuel.

The Lord tells Samuel of His judgment upon Eli, for the evil of the High Priest's sons. *For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not....the iniquity of Eli's house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever.*

They've been made reprobate, cut off for all time from the mercies of God. This again is a picture of the physical nation of Israel, cut off from the true vine which is Christ. Cursed as the fig tree was to never bear fruit again.

Samuel is reluctant to share the vision with Eli, but his master demands it and calls God to curse him if he doesn't tell Eli everything said. Samuel does, and Eli resigns himself to the fate God has judged against him and his family.

teachings.title: Christ is found in every book
teachings.summary: The ordinances show that God's word is consistent across thousands of years and many authors, with Christ as its single theme and the same faith in both testaments.
teachings.text: The details and how each of the ordinances given by the Lord unto the people corresponding to and a picture of the things to come, is fun to study out, but the knowledge of His giving us these things that we may know Him and build in faith, that He is true to His word and His word is consistent, over thousands of years and many authors, given by the Spirit and preserved by God for all time. We can trust His word because He has shown us in it a singular voice, and the theme that is Christ. Everything points to Him. Jesus is found in every book of the Bible. The faith of the Old Testament saints was the same as New; believing on the Lord to save us, a gift given in grace from our Father because He so loved us. That while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. Amen

teachings.title: These things happened for our ensamples
teachings.summary: The repeated accounts in Samuel are real events recorded for our admonition, not folklore, so we can trust the Lord delivers as David trusted Him.
teachings.text:
David continues to show the faith in the Lord to deliver us from tribulation if we remain obedient to Him.

**1 Corinthians 10:11-13**
*Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come. Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall. There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.*

People who criticize biblical fundamentalism and the inerrancy of scripture, or worse, cast doubt on the accuracy or origin of the accounts, will point to the repetitive narrative of **Samuel**, and other books of the Old Testament, to sow doubtful disputations. But we know better. That's Satan's oldest trick.

The Spirit tells us that these things **happened**, and for a reason; as examples and admonition for us, that we understand the will of God for us. So we may know His deliverance is real. So we may trust in Him as David trusted in Him. We can know that these aren't merely stories and folklore, but actual events, and they played out for a purpose, even if it was unbeknownst to those involved at the time. And they were recorded in scripture for us to take heart, to rest easy, knowing that the Lord delivers.

Amen

teachings.title: Preaching Christ from Micah
teachings.summary: Christ could be preached from Micah as Philip preached from Isaiah 53, since the Old Testament is entirely about Jesus and salvation has always been by faith.
teachings.text:
Continuing a thought from the study of Hosea; Christ could be preached to unbelievers through the book of Micah, just as Jesus was preached to the Ethiopian Eunuch by Phillip, using **Isaiah 53**. Micah, like the other prophets, preached judgment for sin, the holiness of God, the truth of His mercy and His Messiah, and redemption by faith in His word, and a call to sanctification and separation for us once saved.

We are blessed to have the clear Gospels, but you can see how there were always a righteous remnant. 7,000 who hadn't bowed the knee to Baal. How the Old Testament was entirely about Jesus and salvation has always been by faith, calling upon the name of the Lord.

teachings.title: All scripture, even Proverbs, is about Christ
teachings.summary: Proverbs carries the gospel that none is righteous, and all scripture including Proverbs is about Christ the Word, through which faith comes by hearing.
teachings.text:
*Most men will proclaim every one his own goodness: but a faithful man who can find?*

There is none righteous, no not one.

*Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?*

As we have seen, the gospel message, the understanding that we are all sinners, that God has made provision for us in His grace, is found throughout the book of Proverbs. Is there any great wisdom? Is there any more perfect truth?

We are constantly instructed to walk in the way of the Lord and to seek after truth. The word of God being a light unto our feet. Jesus Christ IS *the* way, *the* truth and *the* light. He is the Word of God made flesh. To whom all the prophets gave witness. The promise made to man throughout history.

God's word is the Word. All scripture, given by inspiration, is the word of God and all scripture, including the Proverbs of Solomon, are the word, and all are about Christ.

*Mercy and truth preserve the king: and his throne is upholden by mercy.* So there is no wonder that the Bible says;

Psalm 45:6 *Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a right sceptre.*

The infinite mercy and perfect truth make establishes the fact that His throne is forever.

*Man's goings are of the Lord; how can a man then understand his own way?* The Lord calls all men to His way, to follow Him on the path of righteousness, and He uses His word to do so.

*The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, the Lord hath made even both of them.*

Because;
**Romans 10:17**
*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God*.

But those that are dull of hearing, who haven't the eyes to see, remain lost.

**Matthew 13:15-17** 
*For this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them. But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear. For verily I say unto you, That many prophets and righteous men have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them; and to hear those things which ye hear, and have not heard them.*

As Lord, we see the wicked scatter from His gaze, because He brings the wheel over them. We are told, "vengeance is mine, sayeth the Lord," or;

*Say not thou, I will recompense evil; but wait on the Lord, and he shall save thee*

He shall save thee, from all evil. God values true weights and measures, the balances of trade, because He judges with perfect righteousness. Weighing every man. Just so, having an unjust balance is an abomination to Him.

The wisdom of Proverbs isn't only found in the daily application. The understanding that a man of integrity is blessed and his children as blessed after him. A good reputation from honesty is an inheritance. (And a warning that an inheritance can be squandered). Therefore a child isn't only judged by their father;

*Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work be pure, and whether it be right.*

But more than this practical advice, we actually are given a glimpse into the mind of God. To see things as He sees them. That we may walk in His ways and live! Is there anything more valuable?

*There is gold, and a multitude of rubies: but the lips of knowledge are a precious jewel.*

teachings.title: Seeking to be wise, the scholars miss the forest
teachings.summary: Studies obsessed with historical context, Hebrew and jargon miss Christ, the gospel and the prophetic application plain in the Psalms, and should be avoided.
teachings.text:
I want to take the opportunity here, with such a short and concise Psalm, to deal with the way many modern "theologians" approach the Old Testament, and the Psalms in particular.

When I read and react to the text, all I see is Jesus, the gospel, and the clear and present application of worship in our lives, and the prophetic nature, which clearly is reflected in New Testament end times scripture.

Nearly every Psalm is an uplifting song of praise, worship and trust, with the warnings against the wicked and promises of deliverance from their evil, and God's wrath upon them.

Meanwhile, most studies become hyper fixated on the context David wrote them in, the situation he was facing. Often totally invented by the author (or parroting an earlier study of another man).

Seeking to be wise, they become fools. They want to impress the reader with how clever they are and how their "knowledge of the Hebrew" and extrabiblical sources puts them above the normal believer, who may read the plain text and see themselves, and the future promises of God, as the primary application today.

A typical example;

"Actually, Psalm 11 is best understood as David’s response to well-meaning but fearful advisers during a time of personal danger, most likely when political enemies or rebellious forces threatened the stability of his rule. The opening dialogue (“Flee as a bird to your mountain”) reflects counsel to seek temporary physical safety amid apparent societal collapse, while David’s reply anchors his confidence in Yahweh’s unchanging character: the Lord remains in His holy temple and on His heavenly throne, testing the righteous and preparing judgment for the wicked. This likely was written during one of the many crises King David faced.   Notably, the Hebrew of verse 3—kî haššātôṯ yēhārēsûn (“for the foundations are being destroyed”)—employs a rare plural form of šātâ that some scholars conjecture may allude to the subterranean pillars of cosmic order rather than mere institutional collapse, thereby elevating the crisis from the merely political to the ontological; yet even this linguistic subtlety serves primarily to underscore David’s immediate existential plight rather than any distant eschatological horizon."

These men miss the forest for the trees, and create this sterile and unrelatable version of the word, buried under jargon, and with little to no edification or doctrine.

I don't claim to ever exhaust the full meaning and layers of the text in my morning studies. God's word is deep and there are passages that carry a meaning and purpose today, and then read later, convey something totally different. Where the Spirit leads. But when a study becomes an exercise in dazzling the reader with theology, vain philosophy, jargon and concepts that come more from linguistics, semantics and traditions, than the Spirit, I recommend they be avoided.

teachings.title: Dark sayings made plain in Christ
teachings.summary: Parables and dark sayings filter the humble from the spiritually blind, but Christ opened all the Old Testament to show it points to Him, and the Spirit now reveals its meaning to believers.
teachings.text:
The call by David to hear and understand his "dark sayings and parables," brings to mind the way Jesus taught in His ministry.

**Matthew 13:34–35**
*All these things spake Jesus unto the multitude in parables; and without a parable spake he not unto them: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world*.

Jesus revealed to His disciples that parables act as a spiritual filter. To the humble seeker of wisdom, they provide deeper understanding; to the spiritually blind, they remain obscure "dark sayings."

**Matthew 13:10–13**
*And the disciples came, and said unto him, Why speakest thou unto them in parables? He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given. For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath. Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand*.

The unfolding revelation to man throughout scripture was never meant to keep wisdom hidden. Especially, not forever.

Unlike the religions of man, with their esoteric knowledge, vague and shallow sayings fed in dribs and drabs, with no clarity ever given, God's word opens itself up, and Jesus ultimately shows what all these "dark sayings" and prophetic parables actually mean.

 **John 16:25**
*These things have I spoken unto you in proverbs: but the time cometh, when I shall no more speak unto you in proverbs, but I shall shew you plainly of the Father.*

During His earthly ministry, even Jesus' most faithful disciples required His explanation of the parables He spoke in, to the crowds and Pharisees.

**Mark 4:33–34**
*And with many such parables spake he the word unto them, as they were able to hear it. But without a parable spake he not unto them: and when they were alone, he expounded all things to his disciples.*

But the full revelation of scripture came in the days following His resurrection, when all things were finally made known.

To the men He met on the way, in **Luke 24**, Jesus, *beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself*.

And to the gathering of the disciples, He did the same;

**Luke 24:44–45**
*And he said unto them, These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me. Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures*.

He explicitly references the three divisions of the Old Testament, (the Law, the Prophets, and the Psalms, like Psalm 49) and grants them the spiritually supernatural ability to finally see past the "dark sayings" to understand the plain truth of the Gospel.

These things are revealed to us by the Spirit, Who teaches us all things. We are able to see the entire picture, fully revealed in Christ, and the understanding imparted by the Apostles in the Epistles for added clarity and depth. Only the future Revelation of Christ Jesus is still through a glass darkly, (although the gist is pretty clear on timing and events).

We see that the Old Testament scriptures aren't an empty recitation of genealogy, geography and events. They aren't the vain contemplations of man. They are the words of eternal life, and all these were written to point the way to Jesus, and provide us with understanding.

**1 Corinthians 10:11**
*Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.*

Not only does God's word exist to show us His ways, but ultimately it is the tool He has given us to fulfill the Great Commission, leading others to the truth.

teachings.title: The natural man receiveth not the things of God
teachings.summary: The mystery Paul speaks of is Christ plainly revealed, not gnostic secret knowledge, and the things of God are only understood by those quickened by the Spirit while unbelievers stumble in a real spiritual blindness.
teachings.text:
Second chapter of First Corinthians, Paul is still establishing a few things, making certain basic stipulations regarding the faith, before getting to his main topic of settling disputes that have come up in Corinth.

In chapter one, he speaks to the faith they share for salvation, and the fellowship of the sons of God that they should have in that faith and Spirit, given all wisdom and understanding come from God in that Spirit.

That unlike the Jews who ask for signs and evidence and the Greeks logic, but that God's wisdom comes from faith and meekness, that the strengths of this world are weakness, and our weakness, God's strength.

Paul continues this theme in chapter 2. Paul says he was determined when he came professing nothing of the world, but only Christ when evangelizing to them in the first place, and Him crucified. Reminding them he was with them as they heard and knew the truth and accepted it with fear.

Paul humbly says it wasn't his oratory or logic, but the power of the word that convicted them. That word is the "hidden wisdom" of Christ Jesus, written before creation. The reference to "mystery being revealed" isn't gnosticism, but that Jesus being the Christ, "to whom all the prophets gave witness" is the mystery revealed. Christianity is an anti-gnostic religion, in that knowledge of who Christ Jesus is and what He did and why is the great mystery that is told us plainly in the Gospel. It's the entry point to the full enlightenment for the novice, not some secret kept for the adept. It's a mystery, only so far as Jesus identity, and kept only for those prior to His resurrection. *Which in other ages was not made known unto the sons of men, as it is now revealed unto his holy apostles and prophets by the Spirit.*.. (**Ephesians 3:1-6)**

Paul furthers the doctrine of understanding the word. That it is only in those quickened by the Spirit that all things of the wisdom of God are revealed through His word.

*For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of God...But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.*

The wisdom of God is available to all who believe the Gospel and stay in His word. But to those who don't believe, who can't humble themselves to admit they are sinners deserving death, that they are incapable of being  righteous enough to justify themselves through their works or repenting of sin, and that our only hope is the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ, freely given through God's grace, God's wisdom is denied them. They can't understand scripture. They stumble over the word. They are offended, snared, trapped in their own pride. Or blinded by their own rejection of God and kept blind by Him.

If you are a believer who has done any kind of soul winning, preaching the Gospel, or even engaged with others regarding scripture online, you will quickly see this inability to understand by the non-believer. It's often just their own reliance on the wisdom of the world that conflicts with the truth of God's word, but sometimes you see that it is a supernatural blindness. It can be disconcerting to show someone clear verse that is clearly understood, and they cannot see it, no matter how you present it or how many supporting verses you share. The spiritual blindness is real, and further proof of the power of God and His word.

teachings.title: Have ye not read this scripture?
teachings.summary: Jesus rebuked error with scripture because God gave His word to be plainly understood, and those who claim it needs esoteric interpretation by scholars are liars.
teachings.text:
And in a familiar fashion, Jesus again corrects them by citing scripture, have ye not read this scripture; *The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner: This was the Lord's doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes?*

Jesus asks this question and makes the statement that they do not know scripture continuously in His dealings with the holy men of the Jews. It is with scripture He rebukes Satan in the wilderness and it is with scripture that He rebukes the Pharisees and Sadducees and scribes.

It is with scripture that we are told to correct and rebuke those in error today.

To think not of what we shall say, but allowing the Holy Spirit, through whom all wisdom and understanding is given unto us, to bring all things into remembrance that we, knowing the scriptures, will be able to rightly answer our accusers.

It is important to say this as even today, even good men, saved by faith, lean on their own understanding and logic, and are offended by others offering scripture to correct those in error.

But what's missed, I think, is that God, who is a loving God, just and true, and who, the Bible says readily gives wisdom to all who seek it, doesn't think it unreasonable to say "*Have ye not read this scripture?*" to man.

God gave us His word to be understood. He gave us His word that we may know Him. He inspired it, preserved it and sent men of God to preach it, because in His mind He thinks that it is clear and understandable when given the oracles of God. That in Him nothing is hidden.

God finds it reasonable to ask this because it is reasonable to expect those who say they are of God to know the word of God. And that His word isn't some great mystery, but revealed to us if we take the time to know what it actually says. Not of any private interpretation, but the clear word.

Those who say you cannot understand it, need interpretation and scholars to tell you what it means, who claim hidden esoteric mumbo jumbo is the true purpose of scripture, rather than revealing to all men the truth, are vipers and liars, sons of Satan.

Like the Pharisees and scribes, keeping others from the knowledge of the truth, and in doing so, blinding themselves forever.

teachings.title: The meaning of lead captivity captive
teachings.summary: Judges 5 shows that to lead captivity captive means to defeat and take captive the one who would have made you captive, not to free captives.
teachings.text:
Judges 5:12-13
*Awake, awake, Deborah: awake, awake, utter a song: arise, Barak, and lead thy captivity captive, thou son of Abinoam. Then he made him that remaineth have dominion over the nobles among the people: the Lord made me have dominion over the mighty.*

Judges chapter 4 and 5. Tell a story of children of Israel commiting evil, and God punishing them with captivity by an invading army, and their deliverance coming from Deborah, Barak and Jael, by the hand of God.

**Judges 4:1-2**
*And the children of Israel again did evil in the sight of the Lord, when Ehud was dead. And the Lord sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, that reigned in Hazor; the captain of whose host was Sisera, which dwelt in Harosheth of the Gentiles.*

The end result being:

**Judges 4:23-24**
*So God subdued on that day Jabin the king of Canaan before the children of Israel. And the hand of the children of Israel prospered, and prevailed against Jabin the king of Canaan, until they had destroyed Jabin king of Canaan*.

And so in chapter 5 we see them sing a song in their victory, describing the events that had happened in poetic terms glorifying God.

It is in this context we first see the phrase "lead thy captivity captive." By capturing Jabin and defeating Sisera his army, Israel had prospered, and lead captivity captive, the one who was to make them captive became captive. They had turned the tables on their would-be captor.

This is the meaning of the term.

It does not mean to free people from captivity. It means to defeat the one that would have captured them and making them your captives instead.

The Bible defines itself.

teachings.title: Nothing replaces your own reading
teachings.summary: No commentary, sermon or post replaces reading the whole word yourself and letting the Spirit give wisdom for when God calls you to serve.
teachings.text:
I really have to give praise to the Lord and the Holy Spirit for the study today. I began to read Exodus 36 for this morning's study and knowing the content beforehand, I was at a loss as to what to comment on it, what seems like a dry restatement of the building of the Tabernacle, which we'd already covered. By the end of the chapter, I knew.

It is important to study the whole word of God and allow the Spirit to bring those things into remembrance that we need as we do. There is no study guide, commentary, sermon, YT video, Telegram post, meme or any other thing that takes the place of your own reading and guidance of the Spirit to all wisdom and understanding.

We never know when we will be called to serve the Lord the way Bezaleel and Aholiab were. But when we are, it is the wisdom in our hearts the Lord placed there that we should rely on to do what He needs.

**Proverbs 2:6**
*For the LORD giveth wisdom: out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding.*

teachings.title: The word is nigh thee
teachings.summary: Against Zophar's claim that God's ways are unknowable, Deuteronomy 30 and Romans 10 show God's word, Christ, is near and can be known.
teachings.text:
Now the third of Job's friends speaks, Zophar the Naamathite. And he has quite a bit to say along the same lines as Eliphaz and Bildad.

He right away accuses Job of being full of words, full of hot air basically, and full of lies. He says that Job's mockery of the false accusations against him deserves to be answered and he's just the guy to do it, too.

He mocks Job's claim to be innocent of the accusations against him. He tells a grieving man sitting in ash with his hair plucked and skin covered in boils, who's lost everything, you deserve worse than what you've gotten. That God knows Job's secret sin and *that they are double to that which is! Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.*

What a blow.

Regardless of anything else, this is a railing accusation. And he feels comfortable doing it because the other two already have leveled the same, even if they did it in a gentler way.

And isn't this kind of dog piling so typical? Especially the holier than thou hypocrisy and fake piety that comes with those that go along with the crowd on moralizing campaigns.

And again he says something true, that God's ways are not our own and there are aspects to God that we can never understand. So true.

But, we can know God's judgments and His word is ever nigh to us.

**Deuteronomy 30:11-14**
*For this commandment which I command thee this day, it is not hidden from thee, neither is it far off. It is not in heaven, that thou shouldest say, Who shall go up for us to heaven, and bring it unto us, that we may hear it, and do it? Neither is it beyond the sea, that thou shouldest say, Who shall go over the sea for us, and bring it unto us, that we may hear it, and do it? But the word is very nigh unto thee, in thy mouth, and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it. See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil*...

God's word was there present with them that they could know it. In a similar way, as Paul writes to the Romans quoting Deuteronomy, the Word, which is Christ Jesus, also came down from heaven that we may know God's will and be circumcised of the heart.

**Romans 10:5-9**
*For Moses describeth the righteousness which is of the law, That the man which doeth those things shall live by them. But the righteousness which is of faith speaketh on this wise, Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above:) Or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.) But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach; That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.*

But the hyper spiritual hypocrites will always couch things about God's word as being unknowable. That we just can't know for sure what God wants or what He thinks is right or what He thinks is wrong. Unless it's to their advantage. They'll say you can't judge, while they judge unrighteously.

And so, Zophar the Naamathite goes on a long-winded explanation about how Job just needs to repent and everything's going to be great. Prosperity gospel time.

teachings.title: Blessed is the man who meditates in His law
teachings.summary: The blessed man meditates on God's word day and night and bears fruit, while those who attack or downplay scripture, as Satan did with Eve, are chaff.
teachings.text:
The book of Psalms, songs sung by the congregation, musicians and singers, in the called out assembly.

Most are attributed to King David, whose playing of the harp soothe his predecessor, King Saul, and while **Psalm 1** isn't clearly introduced as David's, it follows his patterns of praise and doctrine, and generally is believed to be his. But more importantly, they are of the Spirit, like all scripture, and profitable for learning and reproof.

And much like the poetic wisdom of Solomon, we find the gospel of Christ throughout.

Verse 1 opens with a standard refrain found in **Psalms**; the blessedness of the man, and the understanding that it is by God's grace and mercy all blessings flow, Whose promises are sure.

Here, the promise to bless those who do not listen to the ungodly, the wisdom of this world. Blessing those who do not go the way of sinners, or the scorners.

In many ways, the Psalms reflect the wisdom of the Lord found in Proverbs, and give an insight to the mind and heart of the King, a man after God's own heart.

David contrasts the ungodly sinners and scorners with the man who delights in the law of God. Who meditates upon the word day and night. This too is a frequent theme found in **Psalms**, and it shows the importance of scripture, and its role in the Christian life.

Too often we see those opposed to Christ attacking the inerrant, inspired and preserved word of God. As Satan tempted Eve in the garden, saying "Yea, hath God said?" enemies of God attack His word, because it is the easiest way to cast doubt, or to put false doctrine, vain traditions and damnable heresy in place of the rock which Jesus tells us to build upon; these sayings of His.

Even so-called professing Christian sects and denominations, that make their history, mythology and traditions the focal point of their faith will downplay and minimize the importance of scripture, mocking Bible believing Christians for making it the sole authority in our faith and practices.

But what sayeth the scripture? Those that walk in the Spirit, seeking the blessings of God, meditate in His word day and night. By doing so, we become as a tree planted by the river, constantly fed and nourished. Bearing fruit for God. Not withering and being cut off, as the unfruitful. Prospering in all our ways.

The ungodly have no fruit. They are compared to the chaff of wheat, that blows away in the wind on the threshing floor. Insubstantial. Unfruitful. Hollow husks with no purpose other than to be burned up in fire.

The distinction between the two types of men, the saved believers, the righteous by faith and the ungodly, who do not walk in faith, is made clear.

We will sit in judgment with Christ. We shall be the church of the righteous, the congregation of the elect in Jesus. But the ungodly will not.

*For the LORD knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.*

Just as Jesus asks Martha after the death of her brother, Lazarus:

*And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this?*

David clearly did. The sinners perish. But the righteous in Christ are with the Lord, always.

teachings.title: The transfiguration and a more sure word
teachings.summary: Peter who witnessed the transfiguration says the written word of prophecy is even more sure, and the glory on the mount pales beside the cross and resurrection.
teachings.text:
The glorious story of the transfiguration of Jesus, where Moses and Elijah, as glorified spirits came to Christ on the mountaintop, and God the Father, in a cloud, again spoke to man, that Jesus was His Son, beloved, in whom He was well pleased, and bidding the 3 apostles to listen to Jesus.

Simon Peter, the stone who always manages to say the wrong thing, in his fear and wonder offers to build tabernacles to Jesus and the two prophets to mark the space. Jesus meanwhile cautions them to tell no one of this until after His resurrection.

It is in Luke's account we learn the matter discussed by the manifestations of the holy men with Jesus; *Who appeared in glory, and spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem.*

His time drawing near, Jesus sought comfort and advice from God the Father and He gave Him council by these men.

The core three, Simon Peter, and the sons of Zebedee, James and John were present at the event, which is described in every Gospel but John, not at all in the epistle of James, and briefly mentioned in an epistle of Peter's, where Peter writes that even as he witnessed this event, and heard the voice of God from the heavens, that we should know that the testimony of scripture is even more important.

**2 Peter 1**

*16 For we have not followed cunningly devised fables, when we made known unto you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but were eyewitnesses of his majesty.*

*17 For he received from God the Father honour and glory, when there came such a voice to him from the excellent glory, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.*

*18 And this voice which came from heaven we heard, when we were with him in the holy mount.*

*19 We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts:*

I think most of us would have a similar reaction to Peter at the first, where he wanted to erect Tabernacles and worship there at the mount for the glory he had seen. We would have made a huge deal about this miraculous apparition of long past Prophets, great holy men of God, and God the Father himself declaring from the heavens the Holiness of his son Jesus. As humans how could we not be swept away by this moment?

But when we understand the glory of what was to be done in Jerusalem. The sacrifice. Jesus being made all sin for all men to suffer and die on the cross, descendant to hell for 3 days and three nights, a burnt offering for our sin, and to be raised again in glory on the third day, fulfilling all covenants. God's word made flesh and fulfilled. When we recognize the enormity of this, and the purchase of our salvation, the event on the mount that the three Apostles witnessed pales in comparison.

And Jesus, as he often did, asked them to tell no man until His time came.

teachings.title: Babylon's fall foretold by Isaiah
teachings.summary: Isaiah's precise prediction of Babylon's fall to the Medes shows the sure word of prophecy, so we should listen when the Bible speaks of the end times.
teachings.text:
The burden of the Lord comes upon Isaiah, a phrase familiar from Jeremiah, the word of God given a prophet that he must preach to the people. This is a prophetic vision of Babylon, the empire, and the spirit of Babylon in the end times. The great and terrible day of the Lord.
