teachings.text:
**1 Corinthians 14:18-22**
 *I thank my God, I speak with tongues more than ye all: Yet in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that by my voice I might teach others also, than ten thousand words in an unknown tongue.*

*Brethren, be not children in understanding: howbeit in malice be ye children, but in understanding be men. In the law it is written, With men of other tongues and other lips will I speak unto this people; and yet for all that will they not hear me, saith the Lord. Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying serveth not for them that believe not, but for them which believe*

Just to reinforce this point; that the purpose of the 1st century churches having members who could speak or understand foreign languages was to be as a sign for the unsaved, that they may hear the Gospel and believe, knowing the power of God.

This means that God's word can be translated into all languages and remain powerful and give faith and keep the same meaning. Even if phrased in the manner and custom of the language itself.

All languages are of God. From Babel to today.

The gift of speaking to others that they may be saved hasn't gone away. It just requires some effort. But the same Spirit works in us, that if we begin a good thing for the work of Christ, He is faithful to help us achieve it.

*If any man think himself to be a prophet, or spiritual, let him acknowledge that the things that I write unto you are the commandments of the Lord.*

In other words, if some claim to be better than, more spiritual than others, more "gifted" then this epistle should set them right that they aren't. That these gifts and whatever talent we have been blessed with by God are to be used in an orderly and decent manner, with charity towards all.

teachings.title: A copy of the law for kings and heirs
teachings.summary: As kings were to copy and read the law, believers who will reign with Christ must learn scripture to judge rightly, turning neither to the political left nor right but to God's way.
teachings.text:
*And it shall be, when he sitteth upon the throne of his kingdom, that he shall write him a copy of this law in a book out of that which is before the priests the Levites: And it shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life: that he may learn to fear the Lord his God, to keep all the words of this law and these statutes, to do them: That his heart be not lifted up above his brethren, and that he turn not aside from the commandment, to the right hand, or to the left: to the end that he may prolong his days in his kingdom, he, and his children, in the midst of Israel.*

This command for kings, for those that rule over others in judgement, holds the most application for us today out of the other warnings for future kings.

We who are saved are heirs to the Kingdom. Admonishments and advice given throughout the OT, and New, are given that we may know right judgment. Not only in this life, but in the Millennial Kingdom, where we are to rule and reign with Christ.

This is an often overlooked aspect of our Christian life. We will judge angels. We are called to be part of the hierarchy of God's divine plan. As husbands, wives, parents, children, servants. As men over thousands, hundreds and tens. To judge the fatherless and advocate for the widow. And as princes of His Kingdom.

And the administration of His Kingdom requires men and women of understanding. This is the most important thing about Bible study, learning scripture and commiting the word of God to our hearts. That we may know His will and execute His judgements with mercy, grace and longsuffering. With understanding.

God told whomever would be king of Israel to make a handwritten copy of the law, that they may know it. That he may keep the statutes and in doing so, serve with a humble heart. This applies to us so much today, and it is as neglected as Solomon neglected it in his day.

God's promise is that we will prolong our days on this earth, that would be well with us and with those who he is given us authority over. And authority under.

When we know his commandments and try to keep them, and we understand his judgment and try to see things the way God does, We will turn neither to the left hand nor the right.

We've been trained all our lives to use the left and the right as shorthand for two diametrically opposed philosophies. But the truth is we as Christians are supposed to embrace a third way; God's way. What is right in His eyes rather than our own.

Many of us identify with the so-called right? Because they are correct in many of their assessments of what's wrong and seem to be moving towards a godly return to tradition. But that can only carry us so far. In the end we are not to turn either to the left or the right, but to maintain the straight paths He has set before us. We would do well to remember that as princess of the Kingdom. Sons of the King.

teachings.title: It is always a choice
teachings.summary: Israel chose of their own free will to leave the work undone, and God gave His word as testimony so men would believe, using even their disobedience for His purpose.
teachings.text:
Just to recap the theme going into the **Book of Judges**; God having delivered the people into the promised land commanded them to utterly destroy the inhabitants and to smash down their altars to the false gods they worshipped. The Lord had been with them in every battle (save one, thanks to the abomination of Achan). He had driven out the people that Joshua and his armies went against. He delivered 33 Kings into their hands. The Lord God rained hail the size of boulders, drove men out with hornets, felled the walls of cities with the shout and trumpets of the Israelites.

But yet they did not fully eradicate the Canaanites and others in the land. They resorted to allowing them to stay in tribute. Valuing their gold more than the commandments of God.

They had the knowledge of the will of the sovereign God, and *chose*, of their own will, to ignore His word, to do as they saw was right in their own eyes. Despite all their valiant deeds and the miracles they witnessed while obeying Him, they slacked off in their duty to do that which was comfortable. Easy. To leave the work unfinished.

By their choice. By free will.

And God responded by removing the hedge of protection around them. By allowing them to feel the consequences of their actions. By using these nations as a thorn in the side of Israel, to prove her that they may learn the ways of war, rather than peace. To be a snare with their false gods, so that the glory of God could be known. That in their tribulation they would call out to the Lord for salvation, and He would place His Spirit on a judge He would raise up to deliver them.

The Bible is the record of God's will for man, in Christ Jesus. And it demonstrates that He gave His word as a testimony, that man should believe Him. The Godhead being three persons, that the witness be true, just as the law requires. Jesus appeared resurrected to witnesses that others believed their report. The Spirit indwells believers, that it testify to them they have eternal life, that they may **know**. The Bible exists, inspired and preserved, that we may hear the word and have faith that it is true, and obey His commandments beginning with the gospel of Christ.

It is always a choice. And God uses our choices to His purpose, even when we are disobedient. Even when some don't believe the report. Even when people fall away from the truth.

teachings.title: Alive without the law once
teachings.summary: He shows original sin relies on corrupt versions like the NIV and leads to infant baptism and limbo, while Romans 7:9 shows we die spiritually when we knowingly sin.
teachings.text:
I will note too that in order to wrest **Psalm 51:5** to say that babies are born sinning and carrying sin generationally, they use corrupt versions of the Bible like the NIV;

Surely I was sinful at birth, sinful from the time my mother conceived me.

Just like most other heresies, they need to twist and rend meaning that's not there to create proof texts.

And like most other heresies, they then need to build on their error to make it fit with other verses that clearly contradict their interpretation.

Sinning from birth, where a baby has no understanding of right and wrong, no sinful needs, only to eat, sleep and grow, no need to covet, is an absurdity. But if you accept this absurd doctrine, then you have to deal with the untimely deaths of infants. Miscarriages and still births. Young toddlers dying in their cribs.

If they are born sinning, and carrying the guilt of sin their parents committed, then those babies by necessity are damned.

And if infants without the law or understanding of right from wrong are sent to Hell for eternity, then that cruelty would offend people, especially mothers.

So, to square this seeming injustice with a perfectly just God, the invention of baby baptism, "Limbo," the extension of grace from Christ's sacrifice for sin extended to children to some arbitrary "age of accountability," and other strange doctrines were formed. Even going so far as to extend Calvinistic predestination to the infants, so that either some babies are elect, and others damned (James White), or by God's grace and mercy, all children who die young also happen to be elect (Reformers who know how evil White sounds).

The simple answer is found in **Romans 7:9**

*For I was alive without the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died.*

The simple understanding that, at some point innocence ends, at the understanding of the law, knowing right from wrong, and we choose sin. And when we do, our spirit dies.

God is just. We must choose salvation in Christ, because we all inevitably choose sin. But those who have no capacity for either choice are not slain in the spirit, or in need of having it quickened again.

Infants are in the same state as Adam in the garden, before breaking the one commandment of God. Their needs cared for by others. Incapable of sin until they can willingly transgress the law of God. And afterwards, like Adam. They fall, and learn the knowledge of good and evil. They die to sin, spiritually.

There is no hard and fast rule of what age this happens. There are some who as soon as they gain understanding, choose evil. This could be as young as a toddler. It could be as a tween. It may be that a developmentally delayed or retarded person never fully gains this understanding, while others do and get saved or become wicked.

teachings.title: Elisha's bones and the cult of relics
teachings.summary: One verse about Elisha's bones is twisted by Orthodox and Roman churches to justify relic worship, which scripture calls unclean, showing why doctrine must come only from clear scripture compared with scripture.
teachings.text:
Elisha's death occurs in this chapter, and a miracle concerning the prophet; Moabites invade and while burying a man, they spied a band coming, a s so they cast the dead man into the sepulchre of Elisha, and when he was lowered into the tomb, he touched the prophet's bones and revived.

This one short verse is used, primarily by the Orthodox Church, but by many Roman Catholics as well, to justify their veneration and worship of corpses, skulls and bones. Relics, they say, of "holy men," the "saints." They claim the bones have power, that there is Spirit still invested in them, and that this power can be transferred to those that touch them, pray to them, and worship them in rites and rituals.

This pagan cult of relics, worshiping death, serving the dead things of the flesh, is wicked as Hell. As Proverbs says; *all they that hate me love death.*

They store the skeletal remains, usually of unknown origin but with grandiose claims or being Apostles, certain saints, in special places. Temples of death. In glass cases to be paraded about, being served. Miracles are attributed to these abominations. Forgeries abound.

But Scripture gives no such accounting. A miracle occurred. The how and the why aren't given. Elisha isn't exhumed and carted around to temples. No Israelites lined up to seek to be healed by the relics of a finger bone or skull.

No instruction is given by the inspiration of God to do anything of the sort. In fact, we are told repeatedly by the word of God that to do so is unclean. It's gross.

**Numbers 19:13**
*Whosoever toucheth the dead body of any man that is dead, and purifieth not himself, defileth the tabernacle of the LORD; and that soul shall be cut off from Israel*; *because the water of separation was not sprinkled upon him, he shall be unclean; his uncleanness is yet upon him.*

Most of the profane and false doctrines of Rome that have trickled down to the various offshoots of that false church, come from similarly dubious reasoning, where they take a single verse or incident, remove whatever context exists in scripture, and make assumptions and assertions that rely on the foolish reasoning of man, rather than the clear word of God.

This is why we as saved Christians should only take doctrine from clear, undeniable scripture. Proving all things. Comparing spiritual things with spiritual things. Searching the scriptures to see if something is so.

teachings.title: The stone cut out without hands
teachings.summary: The empires of Nebuchadnezzar's image came to pass, and Christ is the stone that breaks them and the head of the corner, so we cannot doubt God's promises.
teachings.text:
Now **Daniel 2** is a familiar story. King Nebuchadnezzar has a dream that troubles him, and he cannot recall what it was, but seeks someone to tell him the dream and its meaning.

And all the wizards and wise men of Chaldea cannot do this impossible task. The king orders that all his advisors be put to death for their inability to do this, including Daniel and his friends, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah (Rack, Shack and Benny).

But Daniel stays the hand of the man, Arioch the king's captain, by asking him to give Daniel time, and a promise that the Jewish eunuch could find out the kings dream and interpretation.

And in prayer the matter is made known to him by God. And he brings it to Nebuchadnezzar.

That the king dreamed of an idol, a collosal image. Head of gold, chest and two arms of silver, belly and thighs of brass, legs of iron and feet, iron mixed with clay.

And the interpretation thereof,

The Head of Gold: Babylonian Empire

The Chest and Arms of Silver: Medo-Persian Empire

The Belly and Thighs of Brass (Bronze): Greek Empire (Macedonian, under Alexander the Great)

Legs of Iron, the Roman Empire

Feet of Iron and Clay: the Roman Empire divided, and then scattered among the nations.

This is the history that came to pass.

And then we see Jesus. The stone cut from the mountain, without hands. The stone the builders rejected. The foundation upon which is built the everlasting Kingdom. Destroying the kingdoms of men.

**Matthew 21:42**
*Jesus saith unto them, Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner: this is the Lord's doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes?*

*Forasmuch as thou sawest that the stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it brake in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold; the great God hath made known to the king what shall come to pass hereafter: and the dream is certain, and the interpretation thereof sure.*

**Mark 12:10**
*And have ye not read this scripture; The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner*

Peter to the Sanhedrin in **Acts 4:11**
*This is the stone which was set at nought of you builders, which is become the head of the corner.*

Because we know the empires came to pass, and the truth of the prophecy, how can we doubt the promise of God in Christ?

Isn't it marvelous in your sight?

teachings.title: Daniel 7 and the Revelation
teachings.summary: Daniel's vision of the beasts parallels Revelation's end-times events, and his fulfilled prophecies show this one is just as sure.
teachings.text:
As we see, the parallels between Daniel's vision and the Revelation of Jesus Christ details the same end times events, with similar imagery. Governments, the beast, his making war on the saints, the Son of Man, the beast having dominion for time, times and half a time, 3.5 years, the destruction of the beast, the saints ruling and reigning with Him, and His judgment against the beast.

This is the start of Daniel's prophetic writing. The parallels will build from here.

What an awesome God we have, Who calls His shots millennia before. The same man, Daniel, who rightly interpreted the coming empires, now is given a glimpse at the end times. We can know God's word is true because the interpretation of the dreams Daniel foretold to the kings all came true. This prophecy of Christ Jesus and the victory over this world is as sure as the prediction of the Greek and Roman empires given a young eunuch in the 6th century BC. Amen

teachings.title: Blessed are they that do his commandments
teachings.summary: Revelation 22:14 is Jesus' present exhortation to the saved, not a demand for works in eternity, where the curse is lifted.
teachings.text:
**Revelation 22:14**
*Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.*

This verse from the last chapter of the Bible, after John is wrapped up the revelation of Jesus Christ, pulled out of context to claim that in the new Heaven and new Earth we're going to need to do works to stay saved or something....wew. You know, after the resurrection after the glorified bodies after putting on incorruption after receiving that hope... Now we got to start doing works? LOL ok.

Context matters.

**Revelation 22:1-5**
*And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb. In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations. And there shall be no more curse: but the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him: And they shall see his face; and his name shall be in their foreheads. And there shall be no night there; and they need no candle, neither light of the sun; for the Lord God giveth them light: and they shall reign for ever and ever.*

This is the final prophecy for what it will be like in eternity. The curse is lifted. Every man and woman who was saved by faith will be healed and forever be with Christ, amen. What a glorious day.

Imagine trying to then add works, to place that curse of the law back upon us in perfection.

What a wicked thing.

Meanwhile, verses 10-16 are not describing the future. They are Jesus' message to the present. Encouraging we who are saved to keep His commandants, amen.

*I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches.*

People who wrest with scripture, using out of context verses and saying "it may not say this crazy thing, but it is implied!" are always undone by the word of God.

teachings.title: No doctrine on a parable alone
teachings.summary: Fools misuse parables, and no doctrine should stand on a parable alone, as with Abraham's bosom, since Lazarus was carried to Abraham in heaven, not to a paradise compartment in hell.
teachings.text:
Just as the lame struggle to walk, the fool will misuse parables to their own purposes, drawing wrong conclusions and clouding understanding, rather than gaining wisdom.

While God uses parables throughout the Bible, Jesus teaching almost exclusively in parable to the hard-hearted Jews, so many have been used to create false doctrine. Proper application of parables should lay primarily on any explanation given in the text, (Jesus would often expound to the Apostles their meaning) but for those without clear teaching, the context should then be drawn by comparing scripture with scripture. No doctrine should stand alone on a parable.

The most obvious example is the false doctrine of "Abraham's bosom,' taken from **Luke 16's** tale of the rich man and Lazarus. Jesus is using their example to convey a message of urgency to the Jews, to repent and believe the gospel before its too late. To say that the prophets and Moses gave witness to His day, harken to them and believe. That those who don't are Hell-bound, no matter how rich they are. That those with dull ears and blind eyes will not believe, even if one were to raise from the dead.

But that the faithful, even the afflicted and poor in this world, who call upon the name of the Lord, are carried by angels into Heaven, honored and seated with Abraham, the father of faith. To be comforted forever.

The esigesis and natural man logic required to turn this simple (and I believe, true) story into a doctrine that says that there is a place in Hell that's actually a compartment containing paradise, called "Abraham's bosom," and that that's where Old Testament saints went, is absurd.

The embrace of Abraham is specifically to show how even the lowly beggar, covered in sores, whose life was misery and rejection, someone lower than the dogs without the rich man's gate, rejected by the respecters of persons Jesus is addressing, is given an honor that Jews would be envious of. To sit down with Abraham, in the paradise that is God's heavenly kingdom.

As vs 9 says; *As a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouths of fools.*
